articles.titulo: Understanding lymphatic filariasis risk in endemic regions: Associations with preventive behaviours, environmental factors, and other mosquito-borne diseases.
articles.autores: Saputra YA, Siregar RUP
articles.resumo_original: Lymphatic filariasis (LF) remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, where transmission persists despite more than a decade of mass drug administration (MDA). Using data from the nationally representative Indonesia Health Survey (SKI 2023) (n = 520,505), we examined the demographic, behavioural, environmental, and other mosquito-borne disease associations of self-reported LF in Indonesia. We conducted a cross-sectional, weighted analysis of SKI 2023 with multivariable logistic regression and rural/urban stratified models to identify factors independently associated with LF. Overall self-reported LF prevalence was 1.9%. After adjustment, children aged 0-17 years had higher odds of LF (aOR = 1.36; p < 0.001), and females had slightly increased odds (aOR = 1.07; p = 0.001). Skipping preventive drugs under health worker supervision was strongly associated with LF (aOR = 2.49, p < 0.001). Use of pit or open-hole latrines was independently associated with increased odds (aOR = 1.15; p < 0.001). Paradoxically, not sleeping under insecticide-treated nets (≤3 years or > 3 years) was associated with lower odds of LF (aOR = 0.91; p = 0.044 and aOR = 0.83; p < 0.001, respectively). Co-occurrence with malaria and dengue was observed in bivariate analyses (ORs 2.63; 4.31), suggesting overlapping vector ecologies. Persistent, heterogeneous LF in Indonesia is linked to gaps in supervised MDA, inadequate sanitation, and overlap with other mosquito-borne diseases. Strengthening directly observed MDA, integrating WaSH and locally tailored vector management, and enhancing entomological and parasitological surveillance are critical for evidence-based, multisectoral One Health strategies to accelerate national LF elimination.

articles.titulo: Next-Generation Bed Nets to Control Malaria in Côte d'Ivoire.
articles.autores: Sih C, Assi SB, … Cook J (16 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Next-generation long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) treated with more than one insecticide have been insufficiently evaluated in West Africa.
METHODS: In this cluster randomized clinical trial, 33 clusters of villages (1-3 villages per cluster) in Côte d'Ivoire were randomly assigned (11 clusters per group) to use pyrethroid-only (py-only; MAGNet) (control), piperonyl butoxide-pyrethroid (PBO-py; Veeralin), or chlorfenapyr-pyrethroid (CFP-py; Interceptor G2) LLINs. One net was distributed for every two people, followed by door-to-door visits to assist with hanging the nets and to promote their use. The primary outcome was the incidence of malaria cases among children aged 6 months to 9 years over the year following net distribution. Incidence rate ratios compared cases per child-year between clusters randomly assigned to use PBO-py versus py-only nets and CFP-py versus py-only nets.
RESULTS: A total of 25,660 LLINs were distributed to 11,283 households (py-only, n=3797; PBO-py, n=3559; and CFP-py, n=3927). The primary outcome analyses included 549, 551, and 549 children in the py-only, PBO-py, and CFP-py groups, respectively. Mean malaria incidence over 12 months was 1.11 cases per child-year in the py-only group (control), 0.84 in the PBO-py group, and 0.65 in the CFP-py group. The incidence rate ratios were as follows: PBO-py versus py-only nets, 0.72 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.52 to 0.99; P=0.045); and CFP-py versus py-only nets, 0.57 (95% CI, 0.43 to 0.75; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Malaria incidence over 12 months was significantly reduced among children aged 6 months to 9 years residing in clusters of villages in Côte d'Ivoire that were randomly assigned to use CFP-py versus py-only LLINs and PBO-py versus py-only LLINs. (Funded by The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05796193.).

articles.titulo: Dengue virus 1 and 2: Epidemiology, host-virus interactions, clinical severity and integrated control strategies.
articles.autores: Priya S, Malviya R, … Arockiam D (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue is a serious mosquito-borne viral disease caused by four antigenically distinct serotypes of the dengue virus, of which DENV-1 and DENV-2 have been found to play significant roles in outbreaks and severe disease across different geographical areas. This review discusses the epidemiology, host-virus interactions, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, severity, vaccination, and integrated control strategies of DENV-1 and DENV-2. The relevant literature was identified by searching major scientific databases using keywords related to DENV-1, DENV-2, dengue epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical severity, immune responses, vaccination, and vector control; studies were selected for relevance to the review's objectives. The evidence suggests that DENV-1 and DENV-2 share a number of major mechanisms in causing disease, including viral replication, innate immune modulation, endothelial dysfunction mediated by viral NS1, inflammatory response, and antibody-dependent enhancement, but that clinical outcomes are variable and may depend on viral genotype/lineage, prior dengue exposure, host immunity, age, geographical context, and study population. Furthermore, epidemiological and clinical studies have been unable to rank the severity of DENV-1 and DENV-2, as both serotypes have been reported to cause severe dengue across different settings and conditions. The available data thus suggest that the severity of dengue is multifactorial and not serotype-dependent. Ongoing comparative studies that integrate viral genetics, host immune responses, epidemiology, vaccines, and vector control are needed to enhance serotype-specific dengue prevention and clinical management.

articles.titulo: Diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence in early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viral infections: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.autores: Pennisi F, Pinto A, … Gianfredi V (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viral infections is challenging because initial symptoms are often nonspecific and confirmatory testing may be delayed or unavailable. We synthesised evidence on artificial intelligence and machine learning models for the early diagnosis of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420251129670). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to 11 August 2025 for model-development or validation studies reporting diagnostic performance. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were pooled using random-effects models, while sensitivity and specificity were jointly synthesised using a bivariate random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST). Database searches identified 4,531 records, of which 43 studies met the inclusion criteria. The evidence was predominantly from Asia and overwhelmingly focused on dengue; no eligible studies evaluated West Nile virus, yellow fever, or Rift Valley fever. Pooled estimates were 0.954 (95% CI 0.936-0.968) for AUC, 0.904 (95% CI 0.888-0.918) for accuracy, 0.903 (95% CI 0.876-0.925) for PPV, and 0.882 (95% CI 0.859-0.902) for NPV. The bivariate pooled sensitivity was 0.861 (95% CI 0.809-0.900) and specificity was 0.902 (95% CI 0.871-0.927). Heterogeneity was substantial for the univariate outcomes (I2 95.8%-97.7%). Most studies were at high overall risk of bias, while calibration and external validation were uncommon. Artificial intelligence models showed encouraging diagnostic performance in the published literature, but the pooled estimates should be interpreted as descriptive summaries of a highly heterogeneous evidence base rather than as definitive estimates of real-world performance. Prospective, externally validated, well-calibrated, and geographically diverse studies are needed before routine clinical implementation can be recommended.

articles.titulo: Tracking West Nile virus dynamics using viral loads from trapped mosquitoes.
articles.autores: Alahakoon P, Marchinton I, … Hay JA (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne virus transmission is increasing globally. Due to a lack of effective vaccines or targeted treatments, mitigation relies on reducing human exposure to infectious mosquitoes. Entomological surveillance provides estimates of human risk by quantifying the prevalence of arboviruses in mosquito populations. Testing of pooled mosquitoes via RT-qPCR is often used to infer infection prevalence; however, these data are often binarised and ignore semi-quantitative cycle threshold (Ct values) that may provide valuable information on virus kinetics, mosquito infectiousness, and ultimately human risk. West Nile virus (WNV) is a globally distributed arbovirus and endemic to the United States. In this study, we analysed pooled Ct values from retrospective mosquito surveillance and found substantial variation that could not be explained by laboratory factors alone. To understand how underlying viral load and epidemiological dynamics might explain this variation, we developed a multi-scale model linking pooled Ct values to heterogeneous within-host viral kinetics in mosquitoes and birds and seasonal transmission dynamics. Our modelling suggests that Ct values from positive pools might reflect a mixture of potentially infectious and non-infectious mosquitoes, indicating that a substantial proportion of PCR-positive mosquitoes might not contribute to transmission. We then developed a method to estimate mosquito infection prevalence using only pooled Ct values that distinguishes infectious from non-infectious prevalence. Estimates of overall prevalence were comparable to standard methods using binarised data and remained accurate at higher prevalences where standard approaches fail. Overall, these findings demonstrate that entomological viral load data reflect biologically meaningful variation in mosquito infection status that is lost through binarisation. Accounting for heterogeneous mosquito viral kinetics can improve interpretation of surveillance data and estimates of transmission risk, with implications for arbovirus surveillance beyond WNV.

articles.titulo: fruitless is essential for male Aedes aegypti mosquito attraction to female flight sounds.
articles.autores: Loh YM, Thornton AJ, … Kamikouchi A (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Male mosquitoes locate females through strong and innate attraction to female flight sounds, the basis of mating in the world's deadliest animal. In contrast, females do not show any sound attraction behaviors. Despite being documented for almost a century, the molecular underpinnings of these behavioral dimorphisms remain unknown. Here, we found that by disrupting the male-specific isoform of fruitless (referred to as fruM) in Aedes aegypti, fruM mutant males show complete abolition of sound attraction behaviors, resulting in failure of mutant males to locate females for mating. We identified strong fruitless expression in control male ears, with the loss of FruM severely disrupting mutant male ability to amplify female flight sounds. fruM mutant male ears also propagate frequency-specific, sound-evoked electrical signals at about one-sixth the magnitude of control males, significantly reducing the amount of auditory information relayed to the brain. fruitless thus plays a significant role in determining proper male peripheral hearing function underlying mating. Transcriptomic analyses of mosquito ears identified essential hearing genes under the transcriptional influence of FruM via direct or indirect actions, thus shaping male-specific hearing cellular machineries that support male attraction to female flight sounds. Our work demonstrates that FruM commands male-specific hearing behaviors involved in mating by directly controlling the earliest stages of auditory organ performance, sound amplification and acoustic signal detection. Our findings show that FruM is essential for male-specific reproductive behaviors in mosquitoes.

articles.titulo: Hubei virga-like virus 2 in Aedes aegypti: Identification of a conserved 216-bp sequence missing from the RefSeq standard.
articles.autores: Guerrero-Martínez LE, Solís-Vidal S, … Zárate S (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: We report two near-complete genome sequences of Hubei virga-like virus 2 (HVLV-2) from Aedes aegypti in Oaxaca, Mexico. Both genomes contain a 216-bp insertion region absent from the reference sequence but present in all other reported isolates. Split-read analysis and de novo assembly of our samples, along with a reanalysis of raw reads from the reference sequencing project, confirm that this region is present in the original genetic material from which the assemblies were built. Altogether, these findings confirm that A. aegypti is a putative host of HVLV-2 and demonstrate that the insertion is conserved but missing from the RefSeq standard.

articles.titulo: Design, synthesis and larvicidal activity of novel imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole carboxamides against Anopheles arabiensis and in silico target exploration.
articles.autores: Gopikumar IJ, Haroun M, … Deb PK (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Widespread resistance among malaria vectors to conventional insecticides, coupled with the limited availability of insecticides with novel mechanisms of action, necessitates the discovery of new chemical scaffolds for vector control. Anopheles arabiensis is an important malaria vector in sub-Saharan Africa and poses additional control challenges due to its behavioral adaptability and rising insecticide resistance. This study aimed to design, synthesize, characterize, and evaluate novel 6-(4-substituted phenyl)imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole-2-carboxamide derivatives (6a-6i) as potential larvicidal agents.
RESULTS: Novel derivatives were synthesized and evaluated against third-instar A. arabiensis larvae. At 4 μg/mL, mortality ranged from 18% to 97% after 48 h. Compound 6e, bearing a sulfolane substituent, was the most active, producing 93% and 97% mortality at 24 and 48 h, respectively, comparable to temephos (99% at both time points). Its median lethal concentration (LC50) values were 1.17 and 1.03 μg/mL, respectively, compared with 1.41 and 1.21 μg/mL for temephos, corresponding to an efficiency ratio of 0.9 at both time points. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis indicated that the C-6 trifluoromethyl group and polar hydrogen-bond-accepting substituents were favorable. Molecular docking identified adenosine kinase as a potential target, with recurrent interactions involving Gly64, Asn221, and Leu133.
CONCLUSION: The findings identify imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole as a promising scaffold for developing new larvicidal chemotypes. Compound 6e represents the most promising lead and provides a basis for further optimization and validation of this scaffold for innovative malaria-vector control strategies. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.titulo: Extensive mobilome heterogeneity in a widespread endosymbiont: A candidate dimeric plasmid and highly fragmented prophages in Wolbachia from Culex pipiens.
articles.autores: Brunner A, Mahout M, … Reveillaud J (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The obligate, intracellular bacteria Wolbachia have gained increasing interest due to their selfish modifications of host arthropod reproduction, impacts on host evolution, and utility in vector control efforts to reduce arbovirus transmission worldwide. Despite their highly reduced genomes, Wolbachia harbor a rich mobilome that includes phages, insertion sequences and plasmids in mosquito vectors. However, these repeat-rich mobile genetic elements are notoriously difficult to assemble and can generate artificial, chimeric sequences that obscure their true diversity. As a result, conventional genome sequencing and assembly approaches often fail to resolve the complexity, leaving critical gaps of knowledge on how these elements evolve, mobilize, and shape both symbiont and host genomes. To address these challenges, we established a novel Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing strategy that avoids prior PCR amplification and leverages single-dissected, female ovaries. Using this approach, we report and characterize-directly from native long-read molecules-the first near-complete Wolbachia genome and its mobile elements from individual ovaries of the mosquito vector Culex pipiens molestus. Additional short reads from individuals of the same strain were used to assess and validate candidate mutations, particularly in repetitive regions. We report a new dimeric structure of the pWCP plasmid, suggesting the existence of multimeric plasmid forms potentially associated with active replication. We also observed extensive fragmentation of prophage WO regions despite long read sequencing, underscoring their structural complexity. Raw long read analyses recovered multiple alternative gene syntenies within WO regions, pointing to heterogeneous prophage architectures missed by the assembly and marked diversity of WO elements in Wolbachia of Culex pipiens (wPip) group strains. Taken together, our results illuminate the structural heterogeneity of the endosymbiont genome that is shaped by integrated and episomal mobile elements.

articles.titulo: Presence of Heterozygous V1016G kdr Mutation in Pyrethroid Insecticide Resistance in Aedes aegypti a Dengue vector from Southern India.
articles.autores: Anbalagan R, M P, … Krishnan J (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Aedes aegypti is a primary vector of Dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika viruses, and its control relies heavily on pyrethroid insecticides. However, the development of resistance in mosquito populations poses a major challenge to effective vector control. This study aimed to investigate the presence of the V1016G knockdown resistance (kdr) mutation in Aedes aegypti collected from Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu, India.
METHODS: Aedes immatures were collected from selected field sites and subjected to insecticide susceptibility testing using World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. Genomic DNA was extracted, and allele-specific PCR was performed to detect the V1016G mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene (vgsc).
RESULTS: The analysis revealed the presence of the V1016G mutation in heterozygous form (VG) among the tested samples. No homozygous mutants (GG) were detected. The presence of heterozygous individuals indicates an early stage of resistance development, likely due to ongoing insecticide selection pressure. Bioassay results showed reduced susceptibility to pyrethroids in these populations, supporting the molecular findings.
CONCLUSION: This study provides baseline data on the genetic mechanism of pyrethroid resistance in Aedes aegypti from Nagapattinam district. Regular monitoring of kdr mutations is essential to detect resistance early and guide insecticide use policies. Integrating molecular surveillance with conventional control measures will help delay the spread of resistance and improve the long-term success of vector management programs. The findings highlight the need for alternative control strategies and responsible insecticide use to maintain the effectiveness of current interventions.

articles.titulo: Molecular Xenomonitoring of Dirofilaria immitis in Mosquitoes From an Urban Recreational Lagoon in Veracruz, Mexico.
articles.autores: Herrera-Rodriguez K, Ortiz-Carbajal LA, … Ramos JLB (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Canine dirofilariasis caused by Dirofilaria immitis is a mosquito-borne zoonotic disease of veterinary and public health importance. Information regarding mosquito-based molecular surveillance of D. immitis in Veracruz, Mexico, remains limited despite environmental conditions favorable for vector-borne pathogen circulation. Therefore, the aim of this study was to perform molecular xenomonitoring of D. immitis in mosquitoes collected from an urban recreational lagoon in Veracruz, Mexico.
METHODS: Adult mosquitoes were collected weekly from June to September 2025 in Laguna de Lagartos, Veracruz, Mexico, using CDC ultraviolet light traps placed at three sampling sites around the lagoon. Mosquitoes were morphologically identified and individually processed for DNA extraction using a Chelex®-based protocol. Detection of D. immitis DNA was performed by conventional PCR targeting the 18 S-rRNA gene, followed by sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 172 mosquitoes belonging to seven species and four genera were analyzed. D.immitis DNA was detected in 9/172 (5.23%) mosquitoes. All positive samples corresponded exclusively to Culex (Melanoconion) panocossa, representing 10.11% positivity within this species. Sequencing and phylogenetic reconstruction supported the molecular identification of the detected parasite as D. immitis.
CONCLUSION: D. immitis DNA was detected in Cx. panocossa mosquitoes collected from an urban recreational lagoon in Veracruz, Mexico, supporting local parasite circulation and the usefulness of mosquito-based xenomonitoring as a complementary epidemiological surveillance tool.

articles.titulo: An integrated One Health surveillance approach to Dirofilaria spp.: Linking mosquito xenomonitoring, blood-meal analysis and veterinary epidemiology.
articles.autores: Vismarra A, Fozzer M, … Cafiso A (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dirofilaria immitis and Dirofilaria repens are mosquito-borne filarioid nematodes of veterinary and public health importance whose distribution is expanding across Europe. This study developed an integrated One Health surveillance framework combining mosquito monitoring, molecular xenomonitoring, blood-meal analysis, and veterinary epidemiological data to assess Dirofilaria circulation and transmission dynamics. During the 2025 transmission season, mosquitoes were collected by the University of Parma in urban and peri-urban areas and by the Istituto Zooprofilattico Sperimentale della Lombardia ed Emilia-Romagna (IZSLER) in rural areas. Female mosquitoes were morphologically identified and analysed in pools by Real-time PCR for D. immitis and D. repens DNA. Positive pools were screened for West Nile virus, Usutu virus, and insect-specific flaviviruses in order to detect possible co-infection parasite-virus. Blood-fed mosquitoes were individually analysed by mitochondrial 12S and 16S rRNA sequencing to identify vertebrate hosts. Veterinary practices across Emilia-Romagna were surveyed for canine and feline dirofilariosis during 2024-2025. Overall, 11,225 females belonging to eight species were collected and 181 pools analysed. D. immitis predominated in urban collections, whereas D. repens was more frequent in peri-urban and rural areas. Aedes albopictus was the principal positive species in urban environments, while Aedes caspius predominated in rural settings. Humans were the predominant blood-meal host, followed by dogs, horses, cattle, and birds. Veterinary and vector surveillance showed poor agreement, indicating complementary epidemiological information. These findings highlight complex transmission patterns and support integrated One Health surveillance to improve risk assessment and guide evidence-based prevention and control strategies for Dirofilaria and other vector-borne zoonoses.

articles.titulo: Determinants of orthoflavivirus tropism in humans: from cellular entry to organ-specific pathogenesis.
articles.autores: Russow JA, Bertzbach LD, … Pfaender S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Orthoflaviviruses, including dengue virus, tick-borne encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, Zika virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and yellow fever virus, cause a wide spectrum of diseases in humans despite sharing a similar genomic organization. These viruses pose a growing global threat as they are spreading widely, treatment options remain limited, and both climate change and expanding mosquito populations increase the risk of outbreaks worldwide. This review summarizes the determinants of their human tropism, the capacity to infect specific cell types, tissues, and organs. We synthesized current knowledge on how viral factors, including host factor utilization and immune cell trafficking, shape tropism across multiple layers. Central to this process are sequential host barriers that govern infection, including viral attachment, internalization, and replication. Understanding these determinants is essential for informing strategies to mitigate the global burden of these medically important pathogens.

articles.titulo: Integrating developmental traits, morphometrics and machine learning for sex classification of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae).
articles.autores: Hila AMJ, Amalin DM, … Carvajal TM (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Aedes aegypti (Linnaeus, 1762), the primary vector for dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever, requires precise sex separation for the effective application of the sterile insect technique. This study integrates developmental biology, morphometric analysis and machine learning to differentiate sexes in Ae. aegypti pupae and adults. We evaluated developmental parameters across six generations of the Old Balara strain. Morphometric data from pupae and adults, including pupal cephalothorax dimensions, pupal length, pupal weight, adult wing length and adult thorax length, were collected to assess their correlations. Pupal morphometrics (cephalothorax dimensions and pupal length and weight) were used to train nine ML models for pupal sex classification. Males pupated significantly earlier (5.61 ± 0.10 days) than females (6.40 ± 0.16 days). In the absence of mating, females lived longer (22.63 ± 0.42 days) than males (20.13 ± 0.34 days). After mating, longevity declined, with females showing a 10.34% reduction (2.34 days) and males a 32.94% reduction (6.63 days). Across all morphometric parameters (cephalothorax length, width and perimeter in mm; cephalothorax area in mm2; pupal length in mm; pupal weight in mg; adult wing length in mm; thorax length in mm), females were significantly larger than males. Pupal cephalothorax perimeter and area strongly correlated with adult thorax and wing lengths (R2 up to 0.88), indicating their predictive value for adult size. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines and Naïve Bayes achieved 100% accuracy in pupal sex classification on the test set. Integrating morphometric analysis with machine learning significantly enhances sex sorting precision for the sterile insect technique, improving mosquito control efficiency by ensuring only males are released. Future research should explore incorporating image-based data and advanced machine learning techniques to further refine these methods across diverse mosquito populations.

articles.titulo: Genetic Modification Technologies and Microbial Interventions for Mosquito Control: Recent Advances in Biological Strategies Against Vector-Borne Diseases.
articles.autores: Abbasi E
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND OBJECTIVES: Mosquito-borne diseases continue to pose major global public health challenges, while increasing insecticide resistance and environmental concerns necessitate the development of sustainable alternatives to conventional vector control. This review evaluates recent advances in biological mosquito control, focusing on genetic modification technologies, Wolbachia -based interventions, and entomopathogenic fungi.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Literature published between 2000 and 2025 was retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Eligible studies investigating mosquito-targeted biological interventions were critically evaluated through qualitative evidence synthesis and methodological quality assessment.
RESULTS: The included studies demonstrated variable levels of evidence across intervention types. SIT and selected genetically engineered population-suppression approaches produced substantial reductions in mosquito abundance under field or operational conditions, whereas CRISPR/Cas9 and gene-drive technologies remained supported predominantly by laboratory or contained experimental evidence. Wolbachia population-replacement interventions generated the strongest community-level epidemiological evidence, including reductions in dengue incidence following successful establishment. Entomopathogenic fungi reduced adult mosquito survival mainly under laboratory and semi-field conditions. Across interventions, effectiveness depended on ecological context, operational capacity, surveillance, regulatory requirements, and community engagement.
INTERPRETATION CONCLUSION: Biological control technologies provide environmentally sustainable and species-specific alternatives to chemical insecticides. Their successful integration into Integrated Vector Management requires continued ecological monitoring, regulatory oversight, multidisciplinary collaboration, and community engagement to ensure safe and effective large-scale implementation.

articles.titulo: Lack of fitness cost associated to CYP9K1-mediated insecticide resistance in Anopheles funestus, represents a threat to vector control.
articles.autores: Manyaka-Tientcheu CRK, Tchouakui M, … Wondji CS (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Resistance management is critical to maintain insecticide effectiveness in malaria control, and understanding fitness costs of metabolic resistance is key for effective contingency strategies. This study investigates fitness costs linked to two key metabolic resistance mechanisms, CYP9K1 (454A) and GSTe2 (119F) in Anopheles funestus from Central Cameroon. Using DNA-based diagnostic tools, we evaluated fitness parameters, while monitoring changes in resistance alleles frequencies across generations.
RESULTS: Our findings reveal that 454A-CYP9K1 confers fitness advantages, notably through accelerated pupation (RR versus SS: OR = 4.85; P < 0.0001) and extended adult longevity (RR versus SS: OR = 4.91; P = 0.0001). By contrast, 119F-GSTe2 showed no significant impact on the mosquito's life traits. No significant correlation was observed between the expression of CYP9K1 or GSTe2 and life traits such as adult lifespan, larval development (P = 0.2 and P = 0.1, respectively), or oviposition. After 13 generations without insecticide exposure, despite the absence of the homozygous-resistant 454A/A-CYP9K1 genotype, the 454A-CYP9K1 resistance allele persisted at moderate frequencies (0.39-0.32), indicating a slow reversal of susceptibility. Contrarily, a faster recovery of susceptibility was observed for GSTe2, with the 119F-GSTe2 resistance allele declining from 0.14 to complete absence.
CONCLUSION: These findings elucidate how fitness costs shape insecticide resistance reversal. Although removing insecticide pressure can promote susceptibility restoration, the process might be slower for some (CYP9K1) yet faster for others (GSTe2). Moreover, increased vector longevity associated with resistance could enhance malaria transmission potential. © 2026 The Author(s). articles.titulo: Genetic Dynamics and Dispersion Pattern Changes in Aedes aegypti Populations (Diptera: Culicidae) in Yunnan Province, China, over Three Consecutive Years.
articles.autores: Gao J, Zhang HD, … Chu HL (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of mosquito-borne viruses and threatens human health globally. To monitor temporal changes in the population genetics of Ae. aegypti in Yunnan Province, we collected specimens from five sites between 2016 and 2018 and analyzed them at nine microsatellite loci and the mitochondrial cox I gene. Genetic diversity in these populations rose initially and then declined over the study period. The inbreeding coefficient shifted from a heterozygous state toward moderate inbreeding. Ten cox I haplotypes were identified, with haplotypes H06 and H09 prevalent across regions, while other haplotypes were limited to specific regions or years. Clustering analyses demonstrated significant population shifts of Ae. aegypti across the five sampling sites from 2016 to 2018. AMOVA analysis of all Ae. aegypti populations indicated that from 2016 to 2018, the main source of variation was predominantly among individuals, accounting for 76.43%, 65.15%, and 80.36%, respectively. Population dispersion patterns across locations initially increased and then decreased over time. Therefore, continuous monitoring is essential, and particular attention should be paid to intra-provincial spread, especially between port and urban areas.

articles.titulo: New Perspectives in Prevention, Control, and Treatment of Dengue Fever.
articles.autores: Castellar-Lopez J, Gutiérrez Rodríguez YJ, … Mendoza-Torres E (16 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti and is endemic in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. It represents a major global public health challenge because of its rapid expansion and increasing incidence. Clinical manifestations range from mild febrile illness to severe disease with hemorrhage and death. No specific antiviral treatment exists, and prevention has relied on vector control to reduce human-mosquito contact. Although vaccines are available, access remains limited. In the Americas, dengue transmission has intensified markedly in recent years. The largest epidemic occurred in 2024, with more than 12.6 million cases and over 7700 deaths. In 2025, reports showed 4 million suspected cases, including 8966 severe cases and 2207 deaths. This persistent burden may be driven by climate variability, urbanization, mobility, environmental change, and widespread vector distribution, all of which contribute to ongoing transmission and disease severity. These trends underscore the critical need to strengthen surveillance, improve integrated vector management, expand vaccine access, and develop effective therapies to reduce the health, social, and economic impact of this disease. Accordingly, effective preventive and therapeutic strategies are needed to address this persistent and growing threat.

articles.titulo: Molecular Mechanisms of Getah Virus Pathogenesis.
articles.autores: Sharif MU, Liu C, Qiu Y
articles.resumo_original: Getah virus (GETV), a mosquito-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, produces distinct pathological outcomes in different hosts, highlighting that viral and host molecular interactions determine disease phenotypes. For instance, horses typically develop acute febrile disease accompanied by limb edema and cutaneous rash, whereas pigs may experience reproductive failure, fetal infection, and severe neonatal disease. These host-dependent outcomes indicate that GETV pathogenesis involves the combined effects of viral entry, intracellular replication, host antiviral responses, tissue permissiveness, and viral dissemination. The E1/E2 envelope glycoproteins contribute to cellular attachment, membrane fusion, and viral entry, while the non-structural proteins nsP1-nsP4 coordinate viral RNA replication and interact with the host's cellular pathways. Among these proteins, nsP2 contributes to suppression of antiviral responses via TBK1-IRF3 and JAK-STAT signaling, whereas nsP3 participates in replication complex formation and interactions with host factors by disruption of G3BP1-associated stress granules. Genetic variation among GETV lineages is also associated with differences in epidemiology and pathogenic strains, although the causal contribution of individual mutations remains incompletely defined. Functional studies of envelope variation, including the E2-N262 glycosylation site, further indicate that viral surface properties can influence replication and virulence. Despite increasing molecular and epidemiological evidence, important gaps remain in understanding the relative contribution of different entry factors, cellular permissiveness, host-dependent pathogenicity, and the functional consequences of naturally occurring viral variation. This review integrates the current evidence on GETV viral proteins, replication, cellular entry, host antiviral responses, tissue tropism, host-specific pathology, and viral genetic diversity to establish the current molecular framework of GETV pathogenesis and highlight the priorities for future experimental validation and disease control.

articles.titulo: WingShape-Warn: A Morphology-Driven Early-Warning Pipeline for Mosquito-Borne Disease Surveillance.
articles.autores: Chen Y, Wang X, … Wang Z (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Environmental stressors-including climate change, urbanisation, and pollution-are increasingly altering the wing morphology of mosquito vectors. These morphological shifts, particularly in wing geometry, can serve as early-warning indicators for mosquito abundance and arboviral disease outbreaks. However, quantitative wing-shape analysis remains underutilised in operational mosquito surveillance and public health early-warning systems. This Technology and Code article presents WingShape-Warn, a reproducible, open-source pipeline that integrates geometric morphometrics, deep learning-based image segmentation, association-rule mining, and Neo4j knowledge-graph construction to detect, quantify, and visualise morphology-driven mosquito-borne disease risk. The protocol comprises seven steps: (1) stratified collection of mosquito wing images along environmental gradients; (2) image preprocessing and deep learning-based landmark/semilandmark extraction; (3) generalised Procrustes analysis (GPA), principal component analysis (PCA), and Apriori association-rule mining on wing-shape variables; (4) Neo4j knowledge-graph construction linking wing-shape traits, environmental variables, and disease outcomes; (5) design of a morphology-based early-warning rule base; (6) automated report generation with a knowledge-update trigger; and (7) validation via retrospective forecasting and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. WingShape-Warn has been validated on 1200 wing images of Aedes albopictus and Anopheles spp. (2020-2024, five climate zones), demonstrating that wing-shape PC1 explains 42.3% of the variance and predicts mosquito abundance with an AUC of 0.89. WingShape-Warn has been measured and validated on 1200 wing images of Aedes albopictus and Anopheles spp. (2020-2024, five climate zones)-the only corpus measured in this study-demonstrating that wing-shape PC1 explains 42.3% of the variance and predicts mosquito abundance with an AUC of 0.89. Two reporting conventions are adopted throughout: results obtained on this mosquito corpus are reported as measured results, whereas all cross-taxa material is reported as illustrative, literature-mapped examples and is labelled [Illustrative] wherever it appears. An ablation on the held-out chronological test set shows that adding wing-shape PCs to environmental variables alone raises the AUC from 0.74 to 0.89 (ΔAUC = +0.15, DeLong p < 0.001; NRI = 0.21, IDI = 0.14), while a permuted-shape control returns the model to baseline (AUC 0.75, p = 0.62). The U-Net landmark detector reaches a mean radial error of 1.34 ± 0.41 px against manual digitisation under five-fold cross-validation, i.e., below the pre-registered 2 px tolerance and within human inter-operator repeatability (1.12 ± 0.33 px). While the measured validation is currently limited to mosquito wings, the modular "analyze-detect-warn" architecture can be reused or adapted by researchers for other arthropod vectors (e.g., ticks, sandflies) or additional environmental stressors; such extensions are presented here as proof-of-concept demonstrations and require independent validation before operational use.

articles.titulo: Molecular Detection of the -308 G/A Polymorphism in the Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha (TNFα) Gene Promoter and Its Relationship with the Development of Severe Dengue in Patients from Urabá Subregion, Antioquia-Colombia.
articles.autores: Salazar Flórez JE, Sánchez RGP, … Naranjo MA (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue fever is a viral infection caused by the dengue virus (DENV), a positive sense RNA virus belonging to Flaviviridae family. The virus is transmitted to humans through the bite of the Aedes aegypti mosquito. Worldwide, between 100 and 400 million cases are reported annually. The infection in humans can cause three clinical forms, which are related to severity: dengue without warnings signs, dengue with warnings signs, and severe dengue. Genetic variants in genes encoding immune system proteins have been associated with severe clinical forms of dengue, including variants in TNF-α. TNF-α plays a key role in dengue immunopathogenesis, and promoter polymorphisms may influence TNF-α expression and inflammatory responses associated with severe disease. Therefore, understanding host genetic variation may contribute to elucidating mechanisms involved in progression to severe clinical forms. This study explored the association between the TNF-α -308 G>A promoter polymorphism and dengue severity. We included 92 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases: 30 with dengue without warning signs, 43 with dengue with warning signs, and 19 with severe dengue. Genotyping was performed using PCR amplification, Sanger sequencing, and bioinformatic analysis of the TNF-α promoter region. Because of the low frequency of A allele carriers and sparse data, pairwise Firth penalized logistic regression models adjusted for age and primary/secondary infection status were used to evaluate the association between variant carrier status and dengue severity. The TNF-α -308 A allele was detected in a small proportion of participants, with variant carriers accounting for 10.5% of severe dengue cases. Adjusted analyses showed higher point estimates for severe dengue compared with dengue without warning signs and dengue with warning signs; however, the associations were not statistically significant, and confidence intervals were wide. Genotype frequencies showed no statistically significant deviation from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (p = 0.112), and the estimated post hoc statistical power was 11.3%. The TNF-α -308 G>A polymorphism was not significantly associated with dengue severity in this sample. The observed estimates were imprecise and should be considered exploratory, warranting confirmation in larger and more diverse populations.

articles.titulo: A Marine Bivalve (Entodesma navicula) Extract Suppresses the Replication of Influenza Viruses and Flaviviruses in Association with Reduced MLKL Phosphorylation.
articles.autores: Moon HJ, Lee G, … Park SI (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Emerging influenza viruses and mosquito-borne flaviviruses continue to challenge animal and public health, highlighting the need for antivirals that remain effective after infection. This study evaluated the in vitro activity of a 70% ethanolic whole-specimen extract of the marine bivalve Entodesma navicula (ENE) against influenza A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1; A/PR8), A/Wisconsin/15/2009 (H3N2), influenza B/Florida/78/2015, Zika virus, and dengue virus serotype 2. Antiviral activity was assessed using time-of-addition analysis, viability-based cytopathic-effect assays, reverse-transcription quantitative PCR, infectious virus titration, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and flow cytometry. In the A/PR8 model, pre- and co-treatment produced no consistent inhibition. By contrast, post-infection ENE suppressed all tested viruses. For A/PR8, Zika virus, and dengue virus, this activity was supported by reduced viral genome abundance, infectious progeny, and viral antigen expression. In A/PR8-infected A549 cells, ENE reduced phosphorylation of receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) and mixed lineage kinase domain-like pseudokinase (MLKL). ENE also reduced the proportion of cells positive for phosphorylated MLKL within Zika- and dengue-virus-infected Vero E6 populations. These findings identify E. navicula as an underexplored source of post-infection antiviral bioactivity associated with attenuated necroptosis-related signaling. Isolation of active constituents and causal validation in primary cells and animal models are needed.

articles.titulo: Lethal Viral Sepsis/Septic Shock in Getah Virus-Infected Ifnar1-/- Mice.
articles.autores: Bishop CR, Tang B, … Suhrbier A (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Getah virus (GETV) is a mosquito-borne Old World alphavirus that has recently increased its geographic range, particularly in China. GETV causes rheumatic disease in horses, but in recent years its primary impact has been lethal infections in newborn piglets. Herein, we characterize a lethal Ifnar1-/- mouse model of GETV which recapitulates many of the features seen in piglets. These include lethality, high viremia, diarrhoea, and splenomegaly, with histopathological findings aligning with those seen in piglets and indicating severe, acute, multi-organ inflammatory immunopathology. RNA-Seq of spleens from GETV-infected Ifnar1-/- mice and subsequent bioinformatic analyses illustrated a cytokine storm response that included robust type I interferon signatures and a pattern of cytokine/chemokine signatures indicative of viral sepsis/septic shock. Ifnar1-/-mice thus offer a framework and a mouse model for understanding GETV disease in piglets. This model also suggests that viral sepsis/septic shock may be the cause of lethality in GETV-infected piglets.

articles.titulo: Left to cope alone: how pregnant and postpartum women and their newborns manage extreme heat in coastal Kilifi, Kenya.
articles.autores: Lusambili A, Scorgie F, … Kovats S (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: In coastal Kenya, high seasonal temperatures compound structural challenges that include intermittent water access, resulting in health burdens from extreme heat. Women can experience limitations in the coping strategies available to them for protecting their health and wellbeing from high indoor and outdoor temperatures. This paper, drawing on the Climate Heat and Maternal Neonatal Health Africa (CHAMNHA) study, aims to describe how mothers and their newborns in rural Kilifi cope with extreme heat in their daily routines.
METHODS: This qualitative study draws on key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions with pregnant and postpartum women (n = 22), mothers-in-law (n = 19), male spouses (n = 20), community health volunteers (n = 22), as well as frontline health providers, policy influencers, and government stakeholders (n = 16). Participants were recruited in Rabai and Kaloleni Counties in Kilifi, on Kenya's coast, during a season characterised by extreme heat and drought. Data were analysed using NVivo 12, applying a combination of inductive and deductive thematic approaches.
RESULTS: Women described five main strategies for coping with extreme heat. These included reducing or removing clothing, seeking outdoor shade and fresh air, ventilating indoor spaces, bathing and drinking cold water, and reducing or rescheduling daily activities. These strategies were also adapted for infant care. Mothers reduced infants' clothing, moved them into shaded outdoor spaces, bathed or sponged them more frequently, and used culturally familiar remedies to manage heat-related discomfort and rashes. These practices provided immediate but partial relief. Heat-retaining and poorly ventilated housing, unreliable electricity, water scarcity and contamination, and diminishing tree cover limited women's options. Some strategies also introduced additional risks. Sleeping outdoors increased exposure to mosquitoes and personal-safety concerns, while opening windows brought dust into homes. Expectations concerning modesty, women's domestic workloads, and appropriate newborn care further constrained coping and sometimes created tension with older household members. Coping therefore involved continuous trade-offs between short-term thermal relief and social, environmental, and health risks.
CONCLUSION: Pregnant and postpartum women in rural Kilifi manage extreme heat through individual and household practices shaped by cultural expectations and material constraints. These practices offer only temporary relief, increase caregiving demands and, in some cases, shift rather than reduce risk. Responsibility for adaptation therefore falls largely on women themselves. Protecting maternal and newborn health is likely to require heat-health guidance in routine antenatal and postnatal care, engagement of households and community actors, and investment in reliable water, cooler housing and shade.

articles.titulo: Diversity, Distribution, and Plasmodium falciparum Sporozoite Infectivity of Anopheles Mosquitoes in Flood-Prone Communities of Kasese District, Western Uganda: A Cross- Sectional Household Entomological Study.
articles.autores: Kalyetsi R, Lewandowski K, … Reiskind MH (20 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background Malaria poses an ongoing public health challenge for children in Uganda, especially in climate-vulnerable, flood-prone communities. Understanding malaria vector species diversity and transmission measures is vital to guide vector control in these unique environments. We sought to determine the vector species diversity, distribution, and Plasmodium falciparum sporozoite infectivity in flood-prone villages in the Kasese district, Uganda. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study in which we collected adult mosquitoes indoors and outdoors from 154 consented sentinel households using unbaited CDC light traps. Mosquitoes were identified morphologically to genus and species. Adult female Anopheles spp. were tested for P . falciparum circumsporozoite antigen by ELISA. We estimated associations between entomological outcomes and covariates of interest, including place of residence, net ownership, household location and construction materials, and reported history of floods in the previous year. Results Between 19th February and 22nd May 2025, a total of 1,772 mosquitoes were collected in 136/154 (88.3%) households. Adult Anopheles mosquitoes were collected in 54/154 households (prevalence 35.1% (95% CI: 27.9-43.0)). The highest presence of Anopheles mosquitoes was in Karusandara (58%), and the lowest in the more urban municipality area (22%). We documented diversity in known malaria vectors, with Anopheles gambiae s.l. (73.7%), and An. funestus (9.4%) being most common, but also An. pretoriensis, An. rivulorum, An. mouchetti, An. nili, and An. marshalli were identified. Plasmodium falciparum circumsporozoite antigen was detected from three female An. funestus demonstrating a mosquito sporozoite infectivity rate of 1.49% (03/202) (95% CI: 0.48-4.53), and a household positivity rate of 1.95% (3/154) (95% CI: 0.62-5.91) across the study area. Conclusion The varied species diversity may sustain malaria transmission in this region of rapidly changing ecological conditions as a result of flooding. The sporozoite infectivity and household positivity emphasize ongoing transmission of malaria, albeit at a low levels, even during an atypically dry period. There is a need to strengthen implementation of targeted vector control interventions with a focus on flood-prone and low-altitude communities within Kasese District, western Uganda.
