articles.titulo: First Serological Evidence of Exposure to Japanese Encephalitis Virus in Feral Pigs and Sentinel Chickens in Western Australia.
articles.autores: Potter A, Brockway C, … Williams DT (19 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) emerged across mainland Australia in 2022, causing substantial impacts on public health and the pig industry. Its emergence raised concerns regarding potential spread into Western Australia (WA). This study aimed to determine JEV activity in WA with a focus on the Kimberley region between 2022 and 2024. It also examined potential pathways of JEV introduction into the state and the challenges associated with flavivirus serology. An integrated surveillance program comprising targeted feral pig surveillance and sentinel chicken monitoring was implemented across northern WA. Sera were screened using flavivirus ELISAs and confirmatory plaque reduction neutralisation tests (PRNT), while feral pig tonsils were tested by RT-qPCR. Evidence of JEV activity was detected in WA between 2022 and 2024. Serological findings from two feral pigs sampled in October 2022 provided the earliest indication of JEV transmission in the Kimberley region. Sentinel chicken surveillance subsequently identified JEV activity in Kununurra, Wyndham, Halls Creek and Newman during 2023 and Derby in 2024. These results provide the first published evidence of JEV activity in WA and highlight the importance of ongoing surveillance, vaccination, mosquito control and preparedness activities in northern Australia.

articles.titulo: Chikungunya Awareness and Related Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among Nursing Students at the University of Palermo, Italy: A Cross-Sectional Study of Associated Sociodemographic Factors.
articles.autores: Santangelo OE, Provenzano S, … Terranova A (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
INTRODUCTION: Chikungunya is an emerging mosquito-borne viral disease that has become a growing public health concern worldwide. Despite documented autochthonous outbreaks in Italy and the increasing spread of Aedes albopictus mosquitoes across Europe, little is known about awareness of chikungunya among future healthcare professionals. This study aimed to assess awareness of chikungunya and evaluate related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAPs) among nursing students at the University of Palermo, Italy.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in May 2026 among undergraduate nursing students enrolled at the University of Palermo. Data were collected through an anonymous self-administered online questionnaire investigating sociodemographic characteristics, awareness of chikungunya, sources of information, and KAP related to the disease. Associations between awareness and participant characteristics were assessed using chi-square tests and prevalence ratio analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 894 students participated (mean age: 22.33 ± 4.53 years; 72.3% female). Overall, only 22 students (2.46%) reported having previously heard of chikungunya. In a multivariable exploratory analysis, third-year students had a higher prevalence of previous awareness compared with first-year students (PR = 3.38; 95% CI: 1.10-10.36), whereas no statistically significant association was observed for age (PR = 1.07; 95% CI: 1.00-1.15). Mass media represented the main source of information (63.6%), followed by university lectures (22.7%). Among participants who reported previous awareness, responses suggested relatively good recognition of major clinical manifestations, although important gaps were observed regarding vector recognition and transmission pathways. Attitudes toward prevention were predominantly positive, and most participants reported adopting recommended mosquito-control practices.
CONCLUSIONS: Awareness of chikungunya among nursing students was extremely low. Strengthening educational interventions on emerging vector-borne diseases within nursing curricula may improve preparedness, risk communication, and future public health responses.

articles.titulo: Analyzing Bunyaviruses from a One Health Perspective.
articles.autores: Desmecht D, Boshra H
articles.resumo_original: Zoonotic viral diseases continue to pose major challenges to global health, particularly as environmental, social and economic changes increasingly influence interactions among humans, animals, vectors, and ecosystems. This review explores Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), and hantaviruses (HTVs) within the framework of One Health, emphasizing the ecological and epidemiological factors that govern their emergence and transmission. Despite their distinct transmission cycles, these viruses share important determinants of zoonotic risk. RVFV is primarily maintained through interactions between mosquitoes, livestock, wildlife, and humans; CCHFV is sustained within complex tick-vertebrate systems involving Hyalomma ticks, domestic animals, and wildlife, while HTVs are predominantly maintained through persistent infections in mammalian reservoir hosts, particularly rodents. Climate variability, habitat alteration, agricultural expansion, livestock movement, urbanization, and other anthropogenic pressures can modify these transmission systems and create new opportunities for pathogen spillover. Effective prevention and control therefore require integrated surveillance that encompasses human disease, animal populations, vectors or wildlife reservoirs, and environmental conditions. Advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic epidemiology, ecological modeling, remote sensing, and climate-based forecasting provide valuable opportunities for improving early detection and outbreak preparedness. To reduce the burden of these zoonotic viral diseases, a sustained collaboration among human and veterinary health professionals, ecologists, entomologists, environmental scientists, and public health authorities is required. Therefore, a coordinated One Health approach is essential for anticipating emerging threats, strengthening preparedness, and protecting human, animal, and ecosystem health.

articles.titulo: Virome Diversity and Host-Associated Heterogeneity in Mosquitoes and Biting Midges Across Yunnan, China.
articles.autores: Su H, Zhao K, … Chen S (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquitoes and biting midges harbor diverse viruses, but the factors shaping their viromes remain incompletely understood. We analyzed 35 pooled libraries from seven host groups across 15 locations in Yunnan, China, sampled in June 2025, using total-RNA sequencing, viral annotation, phylogenetics, and community analyses. We retained 1295 viral contigs grouped into 221 annotation-defined viral taxonomic units (VTUs) spanning 24 families; 107 VTUs were supported only by protein homology. Banna virus-related sequences, an Aedes-associated flavivirus, and four putative components of a divergent Jingmenvirus-related candidate were identified. Host group was associated with family-level virome composition after adjustment for location and sequencing depth (R2 = 0.213, p = 0.0052), and the association persisted across alternative feature definitions. Culex tritaeniorhynchus showed the greatest cumulative VTU richness, although its ranking changed when library number was equalized. Most VTUs detected in this host occurred at one sampled site, without a significant monotonic distance-decay pattern. This study expands knowledge of mosquito-associated and biting midge-associated viral diversity in Yunnan, identifies representative lineages for further characterization, and documents host-associated differences in the detected viromes.

articles.titulo: MXRA8-dependent chikungunya virus infection in PDGFR + mesenchymal cells increases vascular permeability and facilitates hematogenous spread.
articles.autores: Holmes AC, Alippe Y, … Diamond MS (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Alphaviruses are mosquito-transmitted pathogens in the Togaviridae family that cause severe arthritogenic or encephalitic disease in humans. Swelling of peripheral joints and soft tissues is a hallmark of arthritogenic alphavirus infection, although the mechanism by which tissue edema occurs is not well understood. The cell surface protein, matrix remodeling- associated protein 8 (MXRA8), is a cell entry receptor for several arthritogenic alphaviruses. Global loss of MXRA8 expression in mice abrogates foot swelling and reduces virus dissemination. Here, we demonstrate that specific ablation of MXRA8 from platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFRα) cells, including fibroblasts, phenocopies the foot swelling and dissemination deficits observed in chikungunya virus (CHIKV)-infected global MXRA8 knock-out mice. Edema in the foot requires CHIKV infection of PDGFRα + cells, which enhances both infection efficiency and permeability of endothelial cells. CHIKV-induced vascular leakage requires both MXRA8 expression and vascular endothelial growth factor signaling and contributes to dissemination by enabling virus access to the bloodstream. Collectively, our study establishes the role of MXRA8-dependent cell tropism in CHIKV dissemination and pathogenesis.

articles.titulo: Long-read sequencing reveals genomic landscape of structural variants in a major disease vector.
articles.autores: Ketchum RN, Trotter AW, … Matute DR (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The southern house mosquito Culex quinquefasciatus is a major disease vector for multiple arboviruses, including West Nile virus and St. Louis encephalitis virus. Insecticides are widely used to control Cx. quinquefasciatus populations, but resistant mosquitoes have emerged in numerous locations across the globe, including the United States. Much progress has been made in recent years in identifying insecticide resistance (IR) mutations in various pest species. In most species, these studies have focused primarily on SNPs as they are readily detectable. However, several genomic structural variants (SVs) have been experimentally shown to impact IR in Drosophila melanogaster, and structural variation has been observed in natural populations of vector species at a few genes that may be relevant to IR (e.g., cytochrome P450s). Because most population genomic data are derived from short sequencing reads, which fail to detect a large fraction of SVs, the contribution of structural variants to the evolution of IR and other adaptations in vector species is likely to be underestimated in the absence of long-read sequencing data. Here, we present the first genome-wide assessment of structural variants in Cx. quinquefasciatus from wild populations in Puerto Rico and Zambia using PacBio long-read sequencing. We constructed high-quality genome assemblies for each and found a total of 259,046 SVs which consisted predominantly of insertions and deletions. We found that 154,071 of these variants contained or overlapped genes. Of these SVs, 5,225 intersected IR genes and 56 of these were predicted to result in changes to downstream protein function. Several SVs predicted to severely impact protein-coding genes also coincided with signatures of selective sweeps, highlighting their possible role as targets of selection. Many of these variants would have gone undetected using short-read approaches, underscoring the importance of long-read sequencing for comprehensive population genetic analyses of adaptation to pesticides and other strong selective pressures, not only in insects but across the tree of life.

articles.titulo: Zika virus Pathogenesis and Targeted Intervention Strategies.
articles.autores: Suo L, Fan H, … Lin X (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV), a mosquito-borne member of the Flaviviridae family, is primarily transmitted via the bite of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes but can also be spread through sexual contact and vertical transmission. Infection with ZIKV causes Zika fever and Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS); more importantly, maternal infection during pregnancy can result in severe neurodevelopmental disorders, such as fetal microcephaly. Although the World Health Organization declared the Zika outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in 2016, and extensive research has since been conducted, no approved vaccines or therapeutic drugs are currently available. Recent studies have shown that various ZIKV-encoded proteins participate in host-barrier breaching, regulation of tissue tropism, interference with neurodevelopment, mediation of neurotoxicity, and evasion of type I interferon (IFN-I) immune responses, thereby advancing the development of vaccines and antiviral drugs targeting viral proteins. However, the complete mechanisms by which viral proteins synergistically mediate pathogenesis, the clinical significance of antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) and its prevention and control strategies, and the practical barriers to clinical translation of protein-targeted interventions have not been systematically elucidated. This review is structured around viral proteins as a central framework: it summarizes the molecular mechanisms by which multiple ZIKV proteins synergistically regulate pathogenic processes; reviews the current research basis and response strategies for flavivirus ADE, and outlines unresolved scientific questions; and discusses progress in vaccines and antiviral drugs targeting viral proteins, with emphasis on evidence gaps and clinical translation barriers. By integrating existing findings and unresolved scientific questions, this review provides a research-gap-oriented theoretical reference for basic ZIKV research and clinical translation of prevention and control strategies.

articles.titulo: Seasonal Dynamics, Botanical Origin, and Yield of Apis mellifera Propolis in the Mexican Altiplano: Influence of Precipitation, Phenology, and Harvesting Methods.
articles.autores: Alcivar-Saldaña JJ, Rodriguez-Monroy MA, … Canales-Martinez MM (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Propolis yield and composition fluctuate with environmental factors and hive management. In a two-year longitudinal study (2022-2024), we evaluated the seasonal dynamics of propolis production across two apiaries in the Mexican Altiplano during the dry and rainy seasons. We conducted monthly harvesting using three collector types: black polyurethane collectors (G1), beige polyurethane collectors (G2), and flexible polyethylene mosquito mesh (G3), distributed among 24 standardized Apis mellifera colonies (n = 8 per treatment; 576 repeated monthly harvests). Palynological analysis identified 39 species belonging to 38 genera and 23 families, with a clear predominance of herbaceous and ruderal forms (Brassica rapa as the main pollen type). The overall mean yield was 9.02 ± 0.58 g/colony/month. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) revealed significant temporal variation by month (F11,231 = 28.45, p < 0.001) and season (F1,21 = 14.12, p = 0.001). Propolis biomass showed a clear bimodal pattern, peaking in April (20.25 g/colony) during vegetative bud burst, dropping in July (6.25 g/colony), and rebounding in September-October (9.77-9.92 g/colony), coinciding with leaf senescence and pre-winter nest sealing. Monthly production showed a moderate negative linear correlation with cumulative precipitation (r = -0.422, p = 0.040, R2 = 0.178). Conversely, collector design did not result in statistically significant differences in harvested biomass (G1: 6.88 g, G2: 8.98 g, G3: 11.21 g; F2,21 = 2.14, p = 0.142). These findings demonstrate that propolis collection in the Mexican Altiplano is primarily synchronized with regional plant phenology and constrained by precipitation regimes rather than collector design. Consequently, the practical selection of harvesting devices should be guided by operational handling efficiency, economic cost, and raw product cleanliness, rather than expectations of higher quantitative yield.

articles.titulo: α-Glucosidase and Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) Inhibitory Activities, Larvicidal Potential and GC-MS Analysis of Endlicheria paniculata: A Combined Experimental and Molecular Docking Study.
articles.autores: Araujo JP, Silva LED, … Miguel OG (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Essential oils from Endlicheria paniculata tissues were characterized by GC-MS, revealing a high concentration of sesquiterpenes. Major constituents were amorpha-4,9-dien-2-ol (41.12%) in leaves, β -muurola-4,10(14)-dien-1-ol (43.54%) in wood, and spathulenol (18.56%) in bark. In preliminary single-concentration screening assays, the leaf oil demonstrated preliminary in vitro inhibitory potential against α -glucosidase (98.44%) and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) (97.71%), alongside moderate larvicidal activity against Aedes aegypti (  LC 50 = 61.56  μ g · mL - 1    ). Molecular docking simulations complemented these preliminary biological findings, showing that major leaf constituents, particularly amorpha-4,9-dien-2-ol and selina-3,7(11)-diene, exhibited favorable predicted binding interactions toward Ae. aegypti AChE-1, driven primarily by hydrophobic interactions. Overall, these findings provide theoretical insights and support further investigation of E. paniculata volatiles as potential candidates for vector control research and detailed bio-guided enzyme inhibition studies.

articles.titulo: Repeated detection of West Nile virus in Aedes caspius during an unusually early transmission season in humans in northern Italy, 2026.
articles.autores: Chiari M, Defilippo F, … Baldanti F (28 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In Lombardy, northern Italy, 2026, the first neuroinvasive West Nile virus (WNV) human case was reported on 7 July. Concurrently, high abundances of Aedes caspius and low numbers of Culex pipiens occurred at several surveillance sites. Testing seven archived Ae. caspius pools collected in July revealed WNV lineage 2 in six pools from three independent sites. A virus sequence from Ae. caspius shared > 99.94% nt identity with contemporaneous human-derived sequences. Further investigating possible Ae. caspius vector competence, particularly for WNV lineage 2, is warranted.

articles.titulo: First Record of the Mosquito Aedes koreicus (Diptera: Culicidae) in Croatia.
articles.autores: Vignjević G, Grego B, … Merdić E (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Aedes koreicus, the Korean bush mosquito, has emerged as a significant invasive threat across Europe since its initial detection in Belgium in 2008. Native to East Asia, this cold-tolerant, container-breeding species has established populations in more than a dozen European countries. During entomological field sampling in the Buzet area (Istria, Croatia), two used-tire depots in the village of Štrped were encountered and identified as potentially suitable breeding habitats for container-breeding mosquitoes. Following the initial detection of these mosquitoes' larvae, the locality was revisited four times from March to May 2026. Dippers of different sizes were used to sample larvae in the tires. Of the 132 larvae collected, eight species were morphologically identified. Nineteen specimens were identified as Ae. koreicus and were detected during each visit. The identification of Ae. koreicus was confirmed by molecular analysis. Sequencing and analysis of cytochrome c oxidase I showed high similarity among Ae. koreicus populations across Europe. This finding confirms the presence of Ae. koreicus in Croatia, which could potentially lead to further establishment, and highlights the need for continued surveillance of invasive mosquito species.

articles.titulo: Toward an Integrated Response to Arboviral Threats in the Americas: Perspectives from the Dengue Summit of the Global Health Conference of the Americas 2025.
articles.autores: Espinal C, Becerra-Posada F, … Rodríguez-Morales AJ (19 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue remains the most important arboviral disease in the Americas and a growing global public health threat. The region experienced the largest dengue epidemic in recorded history during 2023-2024, with more than 13 million reported cases in 2024 alone, reflecting the combined effects of rapid urbanization, climate variability, population mobility, persistent social inequities, and weakened vector-control programs. This review summarizes and expands on the principal discussions of the First Dengue Summit of the Dengue Initiative of the Americas, held in Cartagena, Colombia, in September 2025. Major themes included the changing epidemiology of dengue; implementation and development of new-generation vaccines, including TAK-003 and Butantan-DV; advances in digital surveillance, outbreak forecasting, and clinical management; and integrated vector-control strategies. Particular attention is given to Wolbachia-mediated population replacement, supported by evidence from a cluster-randomized trial in Indonesia and large-scale quasi-experimental evaluations in Colombia and Brazil, which show substantial and sustained reductions in dengue incidence and hospitalization. In the Aburrá Valley, Colombia, city-wide deployment in Bello, Medellín, and Itagüí was associated with reductions exceeding 90% in notified dengue incidence where Wolbachia became established. The review also examines mathematical modeling, artificial intelligence, climate-informed surveillance, and integrated public health approaches. Persistent challenges include financial sustainability, healthcare inequities, climate change, insecticide resistance, and heterogeneous surveillance and health-system capacity. Coordinated, multisectoral, sustainable strategies that integrate vaccination, vector control, surveillance, community participation, and healthcare strengthening are essential to reduce the dengue burden and improve regional resilience.

articles.titulo: Evolutionary Dynamics of Rift Valley Fever Virus in Saudi Arabia: Whole-Genome Analysis of the 2000-2001 Outbreak Strains.
articles.autores: Farrag MA, Aljowaie RM, … Marraiki NAY (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV) is a mosquito-borne zoonotic pathogen that causes severe disease in livestock and humans, with epidemic potential and a capacity for geographic expansion beyond its African endemic range. The 2000-2001 outbreak in Saudi Arabia represented the first confirmed introduction of RVFV outside Africa, yet comprehensive multi-segment genomic characterization of the circulating strains has remained incomplete. Here, we performed an integrated evolutionary and molecular analysis of the three complete-genome Saudi RVFV strains (Saudi 2000-10911, Saudi 200010901, and SA01-1322) using publicly available sequences. Whole-genome comparisons revealed substantial nucleotide and amino acid diversity, with the L segment exhibiting the highest mutation burden (182 nucleotide substitutions, 17 amino acid changes), while the NSs region of the S segment accumulated 52 nucleotide and 11 amino acid mutations compared to the highly conserved nucleocapsid domain. Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analyses of all three segments consistently placed the Saudi strains within Lineage C (bootstrap = 100/100), clustering with East African strains from Kenya (2006-2007), Tanzania (2007), and South Africa (2008-2010), with congruent topologies across segments confirming the absence of reassortment. Bayesian phylogeographic analysis of 118 L-segment sequences estimated a mean substitution rate of 1.697 × 10-4 substitutions/site/year (95% HPD: 1.5-1.9 × 10-4) and a time to the most recent common ancestor of approximately 1857 (95% HPD: 1835-1876). Selection-pressure analyses using four complementary methods (MEME, FEL, FUBAR, and SLAC) demonstrated pervasive purifying selection across all three segments, with only sporadic episodic positive selection detected at a limited number of codons (six in L, seven in M, and one in S). In silico glycosylation prediction identified conserved N- and O-glycosylation sites on the M segment, with the Saudi strains displaying a Lineage C-typical profile lacking geographically restricted markers. However, the absence of canonical signal peptides in all sequences warrants cautious interpretation of these predictions. Collectively, our findings are consistent with a single introduction of Lineage C RVFV from East Africa among the sampled strains, with no subsequent reassortment, and that the virus has evolved under strong functional constraints with only rare, lineage-restricted episodes of positive selection. The identified Saudi-specific and lineage-defining mutations provide molecular markers for surveillance, while the high conservation of core proteins supports the feasibility of broadly protective vaccines.

articles.titulo: Oropouche virus attack rate in an urban setting outside the Amazon Basin: findings from a post-outbreak seroprevalence survey.
articles.autores: Cavalcanti LPG, Barreto FKA, … Castro MC (28 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Oropouche virus (OROV) is transmitted by the biting midge Culicoides paraensis. Historically, it was restricted to small outbreaks in the Amazon region. Since 2023, genomic reassortment and human-environment interactions facilitated its geographic expansion, including into urban areas. We estimate the OROV attack rate and identify factors associated with infection in an urban area outside the Amazon.
METHODS: A randomised cross-sectional serosurvey in the urban area of Baturité, Brazil. Households were selected using stratified probability sampling proportional to census tract population; one resident per household was randomly chosen. Participants completed a questionnaire, and serum samples were tested for OROV IgM using MAC-ELISA. Associations were estimated using prevalence ratios (PR) with 95% confidence intervals from Poisson regression with robust variance. Spatial clustering of seropositives was assessed using kernel density and nearest-neighbours.
FINDINGS: Of 392 participants, 212 were seropositive (54·0%). Most infections were asymptomatic/oligosymptomatic (72·6%-154/212). Living near rivers (PR = 1·80; 95% CI: 1·20-2·50) and working from home (PR = 1·70; 95% CI: 1·30-2·30) were associated with higher prevalence of infection. Clustering of seropositivity was found in census tracts close to cultivated and forested areas, and in central urban neighbourhoods.
INTERPRETATION: We show large-scale urban OROV transmission, with attack rates exceeding 50%. The high proportion of infections among low mobility individuals suggests peridomestic transmission and vector adaptation to urban microenvironments. Results highlight the need to incorporate OROV into routine surveillance, outbreak preparedness, and differential diagnoses of acute febrile illnesses.
FUNDING: Health Surveillance Secretariat/Brazilian Ministry of Health, and Japan International Cooperation Agency.

articles.titulo: Concurrent varicella and dengue infection in an adolescent female: diagnostic and clinical challenges in an endemic setting.
articles.autores: Gabot JKS, Sengson RFR, … Han SM (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection and dengue virus infection are common viral illnesses in tropical regions. However, concurrent infections are rarely reported and may present significant diagnostic challenges because of overlapping clinical manifestations, including fever, rash, and hematologic abnormalities.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a laboratory-confirmed co-infection with VZV and dengue virus in a previously healthy 17-year-old female patient from Quezon City, Philippines. She initially presented with a 3-day history of fever and a generalized pruritic vesicular rash and was treated for varicella with oral acyclovir. Despite antiviral therapy, persistent high-grade fever, epigastric abdominal pain, leukopenia (2.8 × 10⁹/l), and thrombocytopenia (85 × 10⁹/l) prompted further investigation on the fourth day of illness. Diagnostic testing confirmed acute dengue infection by positive nonstructural protein 1 antigen and dengue immunoglobulin M test results, while VZV polymerase chain reaction testing of vesicular fluid confirmed varicella. The patient received supportive dengue management alongside continued acyclovir therapy. Clinical symptoms improved, with resolution of fever by the sixth day of illness, normalization of hematologic parameters, and progressive crusting of lesions. She was discharged without complications.
CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the importance of considering dengue co-infection in patients with apparent varicella who develop persistent fever, abdominal pain, leukopenia, or thrombocytopenia in dengue-endemic settings. Early laboratory confirmation is essential to distinguish overlapping clinical features, guide appropriate management, and prevent missed or delayed diagnoses.

articles.titulo: circEPSTI1 regulates miR-942-5p-SERPINE1-AKT1 signaling axis to enhance dengue infection and is suppressed by Tiplaxtinin.
articles.revista: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.autores: Das N, Krishnamoorthy P, … Kumar H (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have recently been identified as crucial regulators of gene expression in various diseases. Their role in dengue remains unexplored. In this study, circEPSTI1 induction was observed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and plasma of dengue patients. The induction of circEPSTI1 is interferon-dependent and enhances DENV infection by sponging the expression of miR-942-5p. The antiviral role of miR-942-5p is mediated by bidirectional inhibition through targeting conserved genomic sequences of the DENV genome of different subtypes across NS1, NS3, and NS5 and the host AKT1 signaling pathway. RNA-seq analysis of DENV-infected circEPSTI1 knockdown A549 cells identified SERPINE1 and AKT1 signaling pathways to be dysregulated significantly. circEPSTI1 relieves the inhibition of miR-942-5p over DENV genomic RNA and the host SERPINE1 to activate AKT1 signaling. The activation of AKT1 signaling facilitates cell survival and enhances DENV replication. The expression of SERPINE1 and circEPSTI1 was upregulated in Dengue patients, and pharmaceutical inhibition of SERPINE1 through Tiplaxtinin inhibits the DENV replication by reducing the expression of circEPSTI1. Overall, our result demonstrates the therapeutic potential of Tiplaxtinin by targeting the circEPSTI1-miR-942-5p-SERPINE1-AKT1 axis in dengue treatment.

articles.titulo: Metabolic Screening and In Silico Investigation of Eucalyptus globulus Essential Oil Bioactives Against DENV-2 Envelope Protein.
articles.autores: Afzal A, Ahmad I, … Mashwani ZUR (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The escalating prevalence of viral infectious diseases poses a significant threat to global public health. Among these, dengue virus (DENV) represents one of the most widespread arboviral infections, impacting nearly 400 million individuals annually, with severe clinical manifestations occurring in approximately 1% of cases, as reported by the World Health Organization (WHO). Extensive research across both academic and industrial sectors has focused on various aspects of DENV, including its molecular virology, epidemiological patterns, transmission pathways, and therapeutic targets. The development of the tetravalent CYD-TDV (Dengvaxia) vaccine marked a critical advancement in dengue prevention. Nonetheless, emerging evidence has highlighted several limitations associated with current vaccination strategies, prompting a growing emphasis on the discovery and development of antiviral agents as alternative or complementary therapeutic options for effective dengue management. A total of 14 major bioactive compounds were found to be highly correlated with Dengue, yielding 70 common targets between dengue and bioactive compounds. Protein-protein interaction and network pathway analysis by KEGG and Metascape analysis show higher degree of correlation for DENV-2 targets. Molecular docking analysis shows that Globulol and Ecalyptol have higher binding affinity with two receptors, 1oke and 1tg8 f DENV-2, with binding energies of -8.3 and -7.6. Toxicity and drug-likeness analyses confirmed the safety of the metabolites for drug development. These findings suggest that Eucalyptus globulus essential oil may have potential in the treatment of dengue fever. However, further in vivo studies using animal models are required to validate its therapeutic efficacy.

articles.titulo: Mapping the Evidence for Oropouche Virus to Inform Research Prioritisation.
articles.autores: Atabani SF, Bosworth M, … Duval D (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Oropouche virus (OROV) infection has gained increasing public health attention due to the ongoing outbreaks in South and Central America. The World Health Organisation (WHO) lists OROV as a priority pathogen for epidemic and pandemic preparedness. This work aimed to identify and categorise the available evidence on OROV to inform research prioritisation. We conducted a rapid mapping review (search date: up to 5 June 2025) to identify primary studies on OROV and categorised these by area of research, study design, and geographic region using a pre-defined framework. Included studies were displayed in an interactive evidence gap map (EGM) to identify any evidence gaps. In total, 269 primary studies on OROV were included and mapped into the EGM. Of these, the majority of data and findings were reported from South America, Central America and the Caribbean, reflecting the geographical epidemiology of OROV. The majority of studies were observational and descriptive, based on specific outbreaks. Limited evidence was found on vector surveillance, viral pathogenesis, diagnostics and immune correlates of protection. No experimental studies on potential therapeutics or vaccines conducted in humans were identified. The findings from our mapping review and EGM highlight the utility of this methodology to rapidly identify gaps in scientific evidence for emerging or re-emerging pathogens with outbreak potential. The EGM can be used solely, or in conjunction with other prioritisation tools, in order to focus investment and research efforts towards priority topics.

articles.titulo: Structure-Guided Design of a Subnanomolar Dengue Virus NS4B Inhibitor.
articles.autores: Laorsatiankul P, Baig MH, … Haider S (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue virus nonstructural protein 4B (NS4B) is an essential regulator of viral replication but remains structurally unresolved, limiting drug discovery. Here, we combine modeling, ligand-based design, and experimental validation to enable structure-guided inhibition of NS4B. Comparative models across all four serotypes reveal a conserved transmembrane binding pocket consistent with resistance mutations. Docking of JNJ-series inhibitors defines key interaction features that guide the development of predictive field-based 3D-QSAR models (R = 0.91, Q = 0.89). Prospective screening of bioisosteric and in-house compounds identifies BNJ-495 as a candidate broad-spectrum inhibitor with predicted activity across all four dengue serotypes. Experimental validation confirms potent activity against dengue virus serotype 2 (IC50 = 0.17 nM) with a high selectivity index (∼37,000). Conserved binding interactions across serotypes support broad-spectrum potential. This study establishes a general framework for targeting structurally elusive viral membrane proteins.

articles.titulo: Synergistic Effects of pH and Temperature on Dengue Virus Envelope Dimers: Insights from Microsecond Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
articles.autores: Ropón-Palacios G, Crespi LGF, … de Araujo AS (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue pathogenesis depends on a conformational rearrangement of the envelope glycoprotein (pE) induced by low pH. However, how pH and temperature cooperate to destabilize the dimeric form of the pE, a fundamental step that enables the formation of the fusion-active trimer, remains unclear. Here, we investigate this synergy for Dengue serotypes of greatest medical relevance, DENV-2 and DENV-3. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed on the microsecond scale, at 28 °C, 37 °C, and 40 °C under pH 5, 6, and 7 using CHARMM36m force fields and complemented by extended coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations for the DENV-2 system at 37 °C and pH 5, and for the DENV-3 system at 28 °C and pH 5, and at 37 °C and pH 7. Our simulations suggest that increasing the temperature from 28 to 37 °C tends to expand the conformational space at neutral pH, potentially weakening dimer integrity through modulation of the interfacial interaction network. Acidification appears to amplify this effect in a serotype-specific manner: in our simulations DENV-2 required pH 5, while DENV-3 responded at pH 6. Additionally, distance and principal component analyses revealed an asymmetric dissociation pathway, termed the "compensatory embrace", observed in both all-atom and coarse-grained models. Structural analyses further highlighted the differences in histidine distribution between the serotypes. Moreover, interaction mapping at 37 °C identified candidate interfacial contacts that may act as pH-sensitive latches, maintaining stability at pH 7 but breaking upon acidification. Collectively, these results suggest a potential hierarchy of physicochemical triggers that may contribute to the conversion of dimer into fusion-competent monomers. These interfacial hotspots and the "compensatory embrace" constitute structurally informed targets that, pending validation under native virion conditions, may guide the rational design of antivirals and immunogens, underscoring the value of long-time scale molecular dynamics simulations as a hypothesis-generating tool in drug discovery.

articles.titulo: Dengue virus-2 triggers Epstein-Barr virus replication in primary B cells by co-opting the IRE1-XBP1 signaling axis.
articles.autores: Deng X, Deng R, … Xu P (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The intricate interplay between co-infecting viral pathogens within a host can significantly influence disease outcomes. Dengue virus (DENV), a globally prevalent arbovirus from the Flaviviridae family, and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), a ubiquitous human herpesvirus, share extensive geographical overlap, yet their potential interactions remain largely uncharacterized. This study elucidates a novel molecular mechanism whereby DENV-2 infection triggers disruption of EBV latency. We systematically demonstrate that DENV-2 infection consistently induces EBV lytic gene expression and viral replication in diverse cellular contexts, including epithelial cell lines and, critically, in primary human B lymphocytes-the principal reservoir of latent EBV. Mechanistically, we establish that the substantial burden of DENV-2 protein synthesis and replication induces profound endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, activating the unfolded protein response (UPR). Through pharmacological inhibition and genetic knockdown, we dissect the three UPR branches and identify the IRE1-XBP1 signaling axis as the indispensable pathway for this phenomenon. DENV-2 infection promotes the endoribonuclease activity of IRE1, leading to the unconventional splicing of XBP1 mRNA into its transcriptionally active isoform, XBP1s. Depletion of IRE1 or XBP1 attenuated DENV-induced BZLF1 expression, whereas ectopic XBP1s expression increased BZLF1 transcription. Our findings delineate a precise virus-host-virus signaling model in which an acute RNA virus engages a cellular stress pathway to promote entry into the EBV lytic program and viral genome amplification. This provides a new paradigm for understanding the pathobiology of dengue fever and the complex dynamics of the human virome.IMPORTANCEThis research uncovers a previously unrecognized molecular dialog between two of the world's most common viral pathogens. By demonstrating that dengue virus infection can awaken dormant Epstein-Barr virus, this study provides a mechanistic basis for the long-suspected but poorly understood complications arising from viral co-infections. We pinpoint a specific cellular stress pathway, the IRE1-XBP1 axis of the unfolded protein response (UPR), as the critical molecular switch. This discovery is significant because it not only explains how an acute viral illness can trigger the reactivation of a latent, potentially oncogenic virus but also opens new avenues for therapeutic intervention. Understanding this intricate interplay could lead to novel strategies for managing severe dengue and other diseases where viral co-infection is a contributing factor to pathogenesis.

articles.titulo: Early Risk Stratification for Dengue Triage Using First-24-Hour Admission Data: A Multicentric Study.
articles.autores: Teotia SS, Jain D, … Budhiraja S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND OBJECTIVES: Dengue outbreaks place substantial pressure on healthcare systems because many clinically stable patients are admitted for precautionary monitoring. Early triage remains challenging because mortality is rare and early clinical features often overlap between survivors and non-survivors.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicentric study of 1,148 laboratory-confirmed dengue patients, including 1,127 survivors and 21 non-survivors, admitted in India between 2012 and 2017. Only variables recorded within the first 24 hours of admission were analyzed. After nested cross-validated LASSO-based feature selection, ten machine learning classifiers were evaluated under three scenarios: default-threshold classification, SMOTE-based resampling, and cost-sensitive threshold optimization designed to reduce unsafe low-risk classification while preserving real-world outcome prevalence.
RESULTS: Default-threshold models showed high overall accuracy but limited specificity for non-survivor identification. SMOTE improved minority-class recognition but altered classification behavior. Cost-sensitive threshold optimization improved balanced performance without changing the original class distribution. The threshold-optimized SVM model achieved specificity of 0.857, sensitivity of 0.914, balanced accuracy of 0.886, and correctly identified 18 of 21 non-survivors. Calibration analysis showed low Brier scores among top-performing models, and McNemar testing confirmed significant classification changes after threshold optimization for most classifiers.
INTERPRETATION CONCLUSION: A survival-centric, cost-sensitive machine learning framework using first-24-hour admission data improved clinically relevant dengue triage performance while preserving real-world outcome prevalence. These findings support threshold-aware machine learning as a practical decision-support approach for risk-sensitive dengue triage during outbreak conditions.

articles.titulo: Clinicodemographic and epidemiological factors associated with dengue severity and outcomes among hospitalized patients in Navi Mumbai, India: A retrospective study.
articles.autores: Bhosle SA, Throat DM, … Khera SB (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND OBJECTIVES: Dengue is a major public health concern in developing countries like India, with rising incidence in urban and peri-urban areas. Disease severity varies from mild illness to severe dengue with multiorgan dysfunction and mortality. To analyse clinicodemographic characteristics and predisposing risk factors associated with dengue severity and outcomes, and to assess duration of hospitalization across different severity categories.
METHODS: A retrospective hospital-based study was conducted among 302 laboratory-confirmed dengue patients admitted to a tertiary care hospital in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, between July 2023 and December 2024. Dengue severity was classified as mild, moderate and severe as per National Guidelines for Clinical Management of Dengue Fever (2023).
RESULTS: Majority were adults (75.2%) with male predominance (60.9%). Most cases were reported during the post-monsoon season. Moderate dengue constituted (64.9%) of cases, while (11.9%) being severe. Elderly age (OR = 4.35; 95% CI: 1.62-11.64) and presence of comorbidities (OR = 2.79; 95% CI: 1.25-6.24) were significantly associated with severe dengue (p < 0.05). Mean duration of hospitalization increased significantly with severity (mild: 4.0 days; moderate: 4.6 days; severe: 5.8 days; p < 0.001). Six deaths (2.0%) occurred among the 302 patients, all of which (16.7%) occurred in the severe dengue group.
INTERPRETATION CONCLUSION: Elderly age and comorbidities were significantly associated with severe dengue. Early identification and close monitoring of high-risk groups, along with timely supportive management and targeted preventive measures, are essential to reduce morbidity and mortality.

articles.titulo: Recent Landscape in Dengue Vaccines: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.autores: Prathapan S, Wdcn A, … Malavige N (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND OBJECTIVES: Although the incidence of dengue has markedly increased with rise in disease mortality, there are currently no antiviral treatments targeting the Dengue virus (DENV), and no vaccine provides complete protection against all DENV serotypes. Two dengue vaccines, a tetravalent, live attenuated chimeric dengue vaccine on a yellow fever backbone (CYD-TDV) and Takeda's tetravalent dengue vaccine (TAK-003), have been prequalified for use by the WHO. However, they induce incomplete immunity against all serotypes, with some safety signals in dengue seronegative individuals. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to assess the vaccine efficacy and the safety profile by analysing the types and frequencies of symptomatic dengue cases and adverse events reported in randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of the TAK-003 and CYD TDV dengue vaccines.
METHODS: To evaluate the efficacy of these vaccines, a systematic review with a meta-analysis was conducted using RCTs published between 2013 and 2024 that were identified in the PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL). The selection was performed by two reviewers independently, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer.
RESULTS: From a total of 306 identified studies, seven RCTs met the inclusion criteria. These included two studies on the TAK-003 vaccine and five on the CYD-TDV vaccine, including a total of 53,593 participants. The TAK-003 vaccine trials involved participants aged 2-17 years and assessed two-dose regimens. CYD-TDV studies included children (aged 2-16 years) and one adult study (18-45 years), employing three-dose regimens. The random-effects model for TAK-003 vaccine reduced dengue risk by 79% (pooled relative risk (RR) 0.21, 95% CI: 0.16 to 0.28), while the CYD-TDV vaccine showed moderate efficacy (RR 0.44, 95% CI: 0.33 to 0.58).
INTERPRETATION CONCLUSION: While TAK-003 and CYD-TDV vaccines demonstrated acceptable safety profiles in seropositive children, CYD-TDV had increased risk of hospitalization whereas TAK-003 demonstrated lack of protection against DENV3 in seronegative children. Given the high efficacy in seropositive children, both vaccines are likely to be effective in preventing dengue in populations with high seropositivity rates.

articles.titulo: Insights into Inhibitory Effects of Lapachol against Zika Virus.
articles.autores: Borjas Reyes SP, Cassani NM, … Gomes Jardim AC (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The reemergence of Zika virus (ZIKV) in 2015 and its association with severe neurological manifestations highlighted the urgent need for effective antiviral therapies, which, despite extensive efforts, remain unavailable. Lapachol, a 1,4-naphthoquinone compound abundant in Brazilian plant species, seems to be a promising candidate as an antiviral agent since its activity against other RNA viruses, as well as other human pathogens, including reported activity against Epstein-Barr virus and inhibition of herpes simplex virus type 1 by a lapachol-derived compound. Here, we investigated the activity of lapachol in inhibiting ZIKV replication by employing the wild-type strain ZIKVPE243. Lapachol exhibited potent inhibition of ZIKV with an EC50 of 3 μM and selectivity index of 50. Mechanistic assays suggest that its main action is exerted through postentry inhibition of viral replication, possibly through the blockage of the catalytic sites of NS2B-NS3 protease and NS5 polymerase. Biochemical enzymatic assays confirmed that lapachol inhibits NS2B-NS3 protease and NS5 polymerase activities, being complemented by molecular docking analyses. A protective effect was noted when cells were treated prior to infection, and lapachol was found to induce ROS formation in vitro, indicating that several antiviral mechanisms may be involved, including the initiation of an oxidative stress response that can affect viral particles. Overall, these findings shed light on the potential of lapachol to be used for the development of ZIKV inhibitors, especially targeting postentry stages of virus replication.

articles.titulo: A High-Content Pseudotime Framework for Morphological Profiling of Dengue Virus Inhibitors from a Drug-Repurposing Library.
articles.autores: Hoffstadt JG, Boisvert SF, … O'Meara MJ (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
UNLABELLED: Dengue virus (DENV) causes dengue fever, a globally prevalent, epidemic-prone disease with no FDA-approved antivirals. Additionally, the available vaccine for DENV can increase the risk of severe dengue fever for those who have never had a DENV infection due to antibody-dependent enhancement. Thus, there is an urgent need to identify DENV antivirals. Drug repurposing, high-content screening, and machine learning were leveraged to efficiently identify antivirals likely to inhibit DENV replication. Using high-content screening in a DENV infection model, we characterized the morphological patterns of NS4B and envelope (E) protein expression over time and developed a viral pseudotime model that predicts infection progression to aid in phenotypic interpretation of drug effects. We then developed a single cell infection classifier for antiviral efficacy and performed high-throughput drug screening of 960 compounds. We identified four concentration-dependent inhibitors of DENV with nanomolar-to-submicromolar potencies: esomeprazole, GW4064, pralatrexate, and LY411575. With our pseudotime machine learning model trained on data from the time-series assay, we scored the concentration-dependent inhibitors to map their mode of action onto time points in the viral life cycle. Our most notable results show that LY411575, a gamma secretase inhibitor, exhibited an IC 50 of 72 nM and reduced percent infection to near the level of the mock infection control. Pseudotime inferences generated mode of action predictions that were supported by time-of-addition experiments, indicating that LY411575 arrests DENV infection before the development of late-stage infection associated morphologies, while retaining activity when added after inoculation.
IMPORTANCE: Our approach reported herein couples high-content screening and a viral pseudotime model as a robust platform for the identification of viral inhibitors with imputation of morphological profiles for large-scale drug discovery efforts. Viral pseudotime models can, in principle, be developed for any viruses or biological processes through a defined life cycle, suggesting that phenotypic time points, or phases, can be mapped across data in a broad range of applications. We report a high-content pseudotime framework for mapping temporal phenotypes and apply it to drug repurposing for DENV antivirals, gaining insight into how the mode of action of the screened antivirals correlates to phases of DENV replication. This study demonstrates how image-derived phenotypes can be leveraged to generate mode of action hypotheses and prioritize antiviral candidates for follow-up studies.

articles.titulo: Protein-Protein Interaction-Guided Peptides Interfere with Early Zika Virus Entry-Associated Events.
articles.autores: Rodríguez-Salazar CA, Recalde-Reyes DP, … Giraldo MI (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) remains a public health concern because of its association with neurological complications and congenital disease, yet no specific antiviral therapy has been approved. Since the envelope (E) protein mediates viral attachment and early entry-associated membrane events, it represents an attractive antiviral target. Here, we used a protein-protein interaction-guided strategy to design peptides to interfere with predicted interfaces between the ZIKV E protein and cellular receptors involved in attachment. After in silico filtering and preliminary screening, six peptides (PZ1-PZ6) were selected. These peptides showed heterogeneous physicochemical profiles, low cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity under the tested conditions, and docking-predicted interactions with functional E protein regions. In HTR-8/SVneo cells, antiviral activity depended on the timing of exposure, with greater reductions in infectious titers during co-treatment and post-treatment. All peptides also reduced titers in anti-adsorption assays, supporting interference with viral attachment or early entry-associated events. Consistently, DiOC18 fluorescence signals were reduced in a peptide-specific manner, particularly for PZ3 and PZ6. Nuclease protection assays showed no extensive exposure of the viral genome, whereas transmission electron microscopy revealed ultrastructural alterations without generalized particle disruption. Overall, PZ1-PZ6 are promising protein-protein interaction-guided anti-ZIKV peptide candidates with activity against early viral entry-associated events.

articles.titulo: Antiviral Sesquiterpene Lactones from Laurus nobilis L.: Inhibition of Hepatitis C Virus and Dengue Virus Replication.
articles.autores: Amen Y, Elsbaey M, … Zoidis G (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Natural products remain indispensable scaffolds in antiviral drug discovery, particularly against high-burden viral pathogens. In this study, two major sesquiterpene lactones, dehydrocostus lactone (1) and costunolide (2), were isolated from Laurus nobilis L. leaves and evaluated for their antiviral potential against hepatitis C virus (HCV) and dengue virus (DENV). The structures of both compounds were confirmed by HRMS and 1D NMR spectroscopic analyses. In subgenomic replicon assays, the molecules inhibited HCV replication in the low-micromolar range (EC50=2.34 μM for 1 and 2.06 μM for 2) with favorable selectivity indices. In full-length HCV reporter systems, costunolide (2) displayed enhanced anti-HCV potency, reduced viral RNA and NS5A protein levels, and enhanced the suppressive effect of the clinically approved NS5A inhibitor, daclatasvir. Furthermore, costunolide (2) exhibited cross-flaviviridae activity, suppressing DENV replication (EC50=5.89 μM in replicon cells; EC50=1.27 μM post-infection in infectious virus assays), and demonstrated cooperative suppression of viral propagation along with reduced glutathione. Mechanistically, these results highlight the critical role of the sesquiterpene lactone core, and the observed enhanced combined activity between costunolide and reduced glutathione is consistent with a possible contribution of the NRF2/glutathione antioxidant axis to its anti-DENV action. Overall, this study highlights L. nobilis as a previously underexplored source of antiviral sesquiterpene lactones and establishes costunolide (2) as a promising lead against HCV and DENV, warranting further investigation across additional Flaviviridae members.

articles.titulo: Efficacy, Immunogenicity, Safety, and Evidence Independence of CYD-TDV and TAK-003 Dengue Vaccines in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.autores: Sanchez-Guanilo JP, Contreras CA, Arce-Huamani MA
articles.resumo_original: Background/Objectives: The efficacy and safety profiles of CYD-TDV and TAK-003 are established, but multiple publications may derive from the same randomized trial population and therefore not represent independent evidence. We evaluated efficacy, immunogenicity, and safety while distinguishing independent trials from overlapping follow-up reports and interpreting absolute effects within each programme. Methods: We conducted a PRISMA 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials and follow-up reports from five databases. Outcomes included virologically confirmed dengue, hospitalization, severe dengue, serotype-specific efficacy, immunogenicity, and safety. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated; immunogenicity and safety were synthesized narratively. RoB 2 and GRADE were applied. Results: Nine reports were included. CYD-TDV reduced virologically confirmed dengue (RR = 0.41; 95% CI: 0.35-0.48) and hospitalization (RR = 0.41; 95% CI: 0.25-0.67). Across two independent CYD-TDV trials, absolute reductions were 23.2 virologically confirmed dengue cases per 1000 participants (NNV = 44) and 12.0-50.0 hospitalizations per 1000 (NNVs = 84-20). In the primary TIDES report, TAK-003 reduced virologically confirmed dengue (RR = 0.28; 95% CI: 0.22-0.35) and hospitalization (RR = 0.10; 95% CI: 0.05-0.18), with absolute reductions of 23.6 and 12.9 per 1000 (NNVs = 43 and 78). Later TIDES reports extended follow-up of the same population. Conclusions: Both vaccines reduced dengue outcomes within their respective trial programmes. Absolute effects should be interpreted according to baseline risk and trial context, not as direct between-vaccine comparisons. The synthesis distinguishes extended follow-up from independent replication.

articles.titulo: Building resilience against the growing threat of arboviruses II: a scoping review of Aedes vector competence, larval and adult bionomics and species distribution in Africa.
articles.autores: Oxborough RM, Kamgang B, … Kristan M (18 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Reports of arboviral outbreaks are increasing, yet there are acknowledged shortfalls in surveillance data and outbreak preparedness on the African continent. The second part of this scoping review features Aedes vector-pathogen interactions, bionomics and species distribution.
METHODS: We reviewed studies published between 1980 and 2023 to synthesize existing information and identify knowledge gaps to guide future Aedes research and control in Africa.
RESULTS: 877 full-text articles were reviewed, 70 featured vector-pathogen interactions, 230 vector bionomics and 394 species distribution. Vector competence studies were limited to a handful of countries, highlighting knowledge gaps regarding urban, bridge and sylvatic vector species competence for major arboviruses. Aedes albopictus was highly competent for chikungunya virus with the E1-226V mutation, which has been implicated in epidemics where Ae. aegypti was displaced. Vector competence was dependent on virus lineage and mosquito population. Ae. aegypti competence to dengue virus was highly variable, whereas Ae. albopictus was an efficient vector of Zika virus for African but not Asian lineages. Discarded tires were the most frequently reported positive breeding habitats, ranking among the top three in 55% of publications, followed by other discarded items (cans, bottles, broken plastic items) and water storage containers; however, the relative importance varied by location. The pupal index was reported less frequently than traditional indices (container, Breteau and house indices), which co-occurred in 84% of studies reporting indices. As pupal counts are a better proxy for adult mosquito production, their wider use is recommended to identify locally important breeding sites for targeted control. Adult vector monitoring has shifted away from human landing catch towards BG-Sentinel and CDC-LT traps which may be less accurate proxies of human-vector contact, but efficiency can be improved using attractants. Ae. aegypti was highly anthropophilic and had a major biting peak before sunset. However, findings of Ae. aegypti biting at night-time and being zoophilic in some locations demonstrate the need for periodic monitoring, given changing environmental conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights how Aedes populations vary in their competence for key arboviruses, their breeding habitats, and biting behaviors across Africa. Understanding these patterns can guide targeted vector control and improve preparedness for arbovirus outbreaks.

articles.titulo: First autochthonous cases of Oropouche fever in Southern Brazil: A case series in a non-endemic area, Santa Catarina, 2024.
articles.autores: Pinto RN, Sá BJ, … Carneiro AJB (17 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
OBJECTIVE: To describe time, person, and place of the first Oropouche fever confirmed in the state of Santa Catarina, evaluating their autochthonism.
METHODS: A descriptive case series study conducted with residents of five Santa Catarina municipalities, who tested positive for Oropouche fever in laboratory tests between April 25 and June 12, 2024. Retrospective samples, negative for dengue, and viable for molecular analysis (RT-PCR) were considered. Secondary data collected during epidemiological investigations and information systems were used. Statistical analysis was performed on SPSS 18.0. Autochthonous cases were defined as those with no travel history 15 days prior to symptoms onset.
RESULTS: Of the 41 eligible cases, 33 participated in the study. Most were female (63.6%), white (63.6%) and of economically active age (78.8%). Most frequent symptoms included headache (93.9%), fever (90.9%) and myalgia (81.8%). About half reported recurrence of symptoms after clinical cure. Most reported exposure to waterbodies (57.6%) and areas with natural vegetation (48.5%), as well as frequent presence of the Culicoides sp. in homes and workplaces. Most lived and worked near environments conducive to vector proliferation such as agricultural areas with banana cultivation. No case reported travel to other federative units or abroad.
CONCLUSION: Oropouche cases in Santa Catarina presented a clinical-epidemiological profile compatible with previous descriptions. Unprecedented detection of the Oropouche virus in the region reinforces the need for timely diagnosis and integrated surveillance for emerging and reemerging arboviruses in Brazil.

articles.titulo: DEVELOPMENT OF A TETRAVALENT DENGUE VACCINE: GUARDRAILS NEEDED.
articles.autores: Kirkpatrick BD
articles.resumo_original: Illness caused by one of the four serotypes of dengue virus (DENV 1-4) is the leading cause of vector-borne disease globally, and 40% of the world's population is at risk. Vaccine development for dengue is complicated by the recognition that the serotype causing an individual's first infection with dengue virus may cause development of non-neutralizing antibodies, which can be associated with a more clinically severe second infection with a different serotype. This concept, antibody-dependent enhancement, has led the field to focus on development of vaccines that concurrently protect against all four serotypes (tetravalent). Three major groups have advanced the first generation of tetravalent dengue vaccines, with distinct formulations and approaches: Sanofi Pasteur, Takeda, and a collaborative academic team including University of Vermont, Johns Hopkins, and the National Institutes of Health. This review discusses the status of dengue vaccine development as well as the critical implications and consequences of dengue vaccine design and development.

articles.titulo: Factors associated with the optimal uptake of intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine: The experiences of postpartum women attending child welfare clinics in three rural districts in the Western Region of Ghana.
articles.autores: Amugi G, Agudey DT, … Chinbuah S (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP) is a key preventive strategy. However, optimal uptake remains inconsistent despite high antenatal care (ANC) attendance. This study assessed factors associated with optimal IPTp-SP uptake and explored the experiences of postpartum women in rural Ghana.
METHODS: A convergent parallel mixed-method study was conducted among 1,155 postpartum women attending child welfare clinics in Jomoro, Prestea-Huni Valley and Ellembelle districts of the Western Region of Ghana. Quantitative data were collected using structured questionnaires and analysed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Qualitative data from in-depth interviews and focus group discussions were analysed thematically to explore women's experiences and perceptions.
RESULTS: Among the 1,155 women enrolled, 812 (70.3%) took three or more doses of IPTp-SP (IPTp3-SP). Knowledge of malaria in pregnancy was high, with 92.7% correctly identifying its mode of transmission and 91.7% identifying ways of preventing malaria during pregnancy. Factors independently associated with IPTp3-SP included age 10-19 years compared with 20-29 years (aOR 2.17, 95% CI 1.21-3.88), gravidity of three compared with one (aOR 2.67, 95% CI: 1.58-4.50), and gravidity of four compared with one (aOR 1.83, 95% CI: 1.02-3.28). Lower odds were observed among uninsured women (aOR 0.36, 95% CI: 0.20-0.64), single women (aOR 0.64, 95% CI: 0.42-0.97), and cohabiting women (aOR 0.52, 95% CI: 0.34-0.79). ANC attendance showed a strong association with IPTp3-SP: women attending <4 ANC visits had lower odds of receiving IPTp3-SP than those attending 10 or more visits (aOR 0.08, 95% CI: 0.04-0.15). Nausea, dizziness, weakness, abdominal discomfort, vomiting and difficulty chewing the tablets affected their experiences and, for some women, willingness to continue treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: IPTp-SP uptake was relatively high. Predictors of optimal uptake include age, education, marital status, gravidity, health insurance status, and number of ANC visits. Women with fewer ANC visits were less likely to receive three or more doses. Reported side effects posed barriers to adherence. Strengthening ANC attendance and counselling on IPTp-SP expected side effects may improve completion of recommended doses.

articles.titulo: De novo assembly of complete Plasmodium falciparum isolate genomes using PacBio HiFi sequencing technology.
articles.autores: Nyarko PB, Quenu M, … Claessens A (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Plasmodium falciparum possesses a highly structured genome with extensive sequence diversity concentrated in Variant Surface Antigen (VSA) families. These genes-var, rif, and stevor-play key roles in immune evasion and pathogenesis and are difficult to assemble using short-read sequencing technologies. Here, we applied PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing to generate high-quality de novo genome assemblies from 43 P. falciparum parasite cultures originating from community cases in The Gambia. Parasites were culture-adapted, cloned by limiting dilution where possible, and sequenced using high molecular weight DNA extracts. Assemblies from single-genotype lineages were constructed using hifiasm, producing complete chromosomal-length scaffolds with high base accuracy without requiring short-read polishing. We recovered full repertoires of var, rif, and stevor genes and classified them into known subgroups. Together, our results demonstrate that PacBio HiFi sequencing enables accurate assembly of complex P. falciparum genomes from natural infections. This work provides a valuable genomic resource for future studies of parasite evolution, transmission dynamics, and antigenic diversity, and suggests that VSA repertoires can serve as reliable proxies of genetic relatedness across infections.

articles.titulo: Persistent Non-Falciparum Malaria in Kenya: Evidence from 17 Years of Sentinel Surveillance.
articles.autores: Mwalo MA, Chemwor GC, … Akala HM (23 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Human malaria is caused by several Plasmodium species, including P. falciparum, P. malariae, P. ovalecurtisi, P. ovalewallikeri, P. vivax, and P. knowlesi. Pf is the most virulent and the primary target of most interventions, although mixed-species infections are common. Non-falciparum species are more difficult to diagnose, treat, control, and eliminate. This study aimed to determine the burden of Plasmodium species among symptomatic individuals in selected regions of Kenya.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between 2008 and 2025, a total of 4,255 blood samples were collected from symptomatic individuals presenting at healthcare facilities across 7 sentinel sites, namely, Busia, Kericho, Kisii, Kisumu, Kombewa, Malindi, and Marigat, and were analyzed for species composition via qPCR.
RESULTS: Plasmodium falciparum was dominant in 4,139/4,255 (97.3% 95% CI 0.96-0.97), followed by P. ovalewallikeri 545/4,255 (12.8% 95% CI 0.11-0.13), P. malariae 235/4,255 (5.5% 95% CI 0.04-0.06), and P. ovalecurtisi 217/4,255 (5.1% 95% CI 0.04-0.05). Up to 3,460/4,255 (81.3%) were single-species infections. Between 2008 and 2025, P. falciparum remained the dominant species across all study sites, while mixed infections involving Plasmodium malariae, Plasmodium ovalecurtisi, and Plasmodium ovalewallikeri occurred intermittently at varying frequencies, indicating sustained transmission of non-falciparum species. The geographic distribution of Plasmodium single-species and mixed-species varied significantly across surveillance sites (x2  P = .000) with the Lake endemic region showing the greatest species diversity.
CONCLUSIONS: Although Plasmodium falciparum remained the predominant species among symptomatic individuals, non-falciparum parasites, including Plasmodium malariae, Plasmodium ovalecurtisi, and Plasmodium ovalewallikeri, were consistently detected. The occurrence of mixed infections indicates persistent but low-level transmission of these species. These findings underscore the importance of sensitive multi-species diagnostic and surveillance approaches to better inform malaria control and elimination strategies.

articles.titulo: The relationship between cross-reactive Plasmodium vivax antibody responses and P. knowlesi parasitaemia and clearance.
articles.autores: Rathnam JTT, Rajasekhar M, … Simpson JA (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background Pre-existing antibodies to Plasmodium vivax may cross-react with P. knowlesi and influence infection outcomes. We investigated whether baseline P. vivax antibody levels affect parasitaemia and clearance in knowlesi malaria. Methods Total IgG to 21 P. vivax antigens was quantified in pre-treatment plasma from patients in three Malaysian clinical trials. Parasitaemia was assessed 6-hourly by microscopy and clearance half-life estimated. Antibody associations with P. knowlesi baseline parasitaemia and clearance were identified using regression and machine learning approaches (elastic net regression and random forests). Results Data were available for 134 patients (median age 37 years, 37% with prior malaria). Five antibodies were associated with reduced baseline P. knowlesi parasitaemia (0.75-0.90-fold lower per two-fold increase, 95% CIs ranging from 0.65-1.00). Median P. knowlesi parasite clearance half-life was 2.6 hours (IQR 2.1-3.2). Two antibodies were associated with slightly slower parasite clearance (1.04-fold increases in mean clearance half-life per two-fold antibody level). Within-group correlation analyses revealed widespread, positive antibody associations in P. knowlesi infections, with weaker but coordinated (RBP and DBP family) responses in malaria-negative endemic controls. Conclusions Cross-reactive P. vivax antibodies may partially constrain P. knowlesi parasitaemia, but functional studies are needed to clarify their role in immunity and zoonotic transmission.

articles.titulo: Repeated malaria exposure reprograms Vδ2+ γδ T cell chromatin accessibility and immune function toward a reversible hyporesponsive state.
articles.autores: Press KD, Joseph Maran MI, … Jagannathan P (23 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Vδ2+ γδ T cells contribute to antimalarial immunity via pro-inflammatory and cytotoxic mechanisms. Among children who have experienced repeated episodes of malaria, Vδ2+ T cells develop reduced pro-inflammatory function through mechanisms that remain unknown. We hypothesized that recurrent malaria drives coordinated epigenetic and transcriptional remodeling of these semi-innate cells. Using PBMC from Ugandan children in cohorts spanning high and low transmission (10 children) and longitudinally across a marked decline in transmission (20 children, 3 timepoints), we profiled the epigenome and transcriptome of Vδ2+ T cells by paired bulk ATAC-seq and RNA-seq and by CITE-seq. Higher malaria exposure was associated with reduced Vδ2+ T cell TNFα and IFNγ production and with thousands of differentially accessible chromatin regions. Immunoregulatory genes including LYN , PLCG2 , and HAVCR2 (Tim-3) showed increased chromatin accessibility and/or expression at high exposure, whereas pro-inflammatory gene ( IFNG, GZMK, IL7R ) and AP-1 (JUN/FOS) motif accessibility were increased at low exposure; linkage of regulatory elements with target genes corroborated these associations. Single-cell transcriptional analysis identified a cytotoxic CD8+CD16+CD57+ Vδ2+ T cell subset. In our in vitro model, repeated stimulation with malaria-infected red blood cells or the phosphoantigen HMBPP was similarly associated with reduced Vδ2+ T cell degranulation and cytokine production. Diminished responsiveness was predominantly TCR-dependent, accompanied by heightened p38 signaling, and was partially reversed by rest induced by the tyrosine kinase inhibitor dasatinib. Together these data reveal how repeated malaria may reshape cellular immunity by reprogramming Vδ2+ T cells toward a reversible, hyporesponsive state and highlight targets for therapeutically restoring their function.

articles.titulo: Twenty-Year Trends in Malaria Epidemiology, Importation Dynamics, and Surveillance in Oman: A Retrospective National Surveillance Study.
articles.autores: Ahmed M, Alharbi B, … Al Kiyumi R (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
BACKGROUND: Malaria remains a major vector-borne disease worldwide. Oman interrupted endemic malaria transmission in 2010, but imported infections and occasional locally acquired cases continue to require sustained surveillance. This study evaluated national malaria epidemiology and surveillance patterns across the complete 2005-2024 period.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational analysis of aggregated malaria surveillance indicators reported by the Oman Ministry of Health and linked national surveillance sources. The analytical series comprised 20 consecutive annual observations (2005-2024). Indicators included Annual Parasite Incidence (API), Slide Positivity Rate (SPR), Annual Blood Examination Rate (ABER), blood slides examined, case origin, surveillance approach, Plasmodium species distribution, and 2024 governorate-level case counts. Descriptive analyses, linear temporal models, robust Poisson rate models, regression diagnostics with Newey-West sensitivity analyses, and a 2024 population-referenced geographic analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Across all 20 years, 17,080 malaria cases were reported; 16,905 (98.98%) were imported, 174 (1.02%) were autochthonous, and one case was unclassified by origin. API declined from 0.217 per 1000 population in 2005 to 0.064 in 2024. ABER and annual blood-slide examination volume declined, whereas SPR increased over time. The temporal slope for blood slides examined was strongly negative (standardized β = -0.907, p < 0.001). The annual testing-volume-SPR association was inverse and statistically significant in the restored 20-year series (B = -0.00000147, 95% CI -0.00000254 to -0.00000040, p = 0.010; R2 = 0.317); the association remained significant with Newey-West lag-1 standard errors (p = 0.019). Among the two principal species, the relative annual rate of P. falciparum increased (aRR = 1.142, 95% CI 1.068-1.221, p < 0.001), whereas that of P. vivax decreased (aRR = 0.952, 95% CI 0.919-0.987, p = 0.007). In 2024, crude reported case rates varied across governorates, but these rates combine imported and locally acquired cases and therefore do not represent local transmission incidence.
CONCLUSION: Surveillance during 2005-2024 was characterized by persistent predominance of imported malaria, sparse autochthonous cases, changing species composition, and declining testing-volume indicators. The findings support continued diagnostic readiness and surveillance for imported infection and possible re-establishment, without implying effectiveness of any specific intervention.

articles.titulo: Evolution of Neuroparasitic Infections in the South of Madrid Region, Spain: A Hospital-Based Study.
articles.autores: Antón-Berenguer V, Ligero-López J, … Rubio Muñoz JM (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Parasitic infections of the central nervous system (CNS) constitute a diverse group of diseases, many of which the World Health Organization classifies as neglected tropical diseases. This study aimed to analyze trends in diagnosis, clinical profile, and epidemiology of these infections through a retrospective review of cases at a secondary hospital in southern Madrid, Spain, from January 1992 to December 2024. Among the 74 patients diagnosed, 58 (78.4%) had neurotoxoplasmosis (NT), 14 (18.9%) neurocysticercosis (NC), and the remaining two cases were cerebral malaria and disseminated amoebiasis with CNS involvement. Diagnosis primarily relied on neuroimaging, which suggested differences in parasite locations within the CNS. All NT patients were HIV-associated immunocompromised, whereas all NC patients were immunocompetent. NT incidence has declined substantially since the late 20th century, following the introduction of highly active antiretroviral therapy, which has also reduced recurrences and mortality. Conversely, NC shifted from a locally endemic disease to an imported one, with all cases diagnosed after 2001 involving patients from Latin America, reflecting both the success of Taenia solium control measures in Spain and the impact of migration. These findings underscore the importance of epidemiological surveillance and control strategies tailored to at-risk populations and the demographic shifts associated with migration.

articles.titulo: Synthesis, Characterization and Structural Elucidation of Biocompatible Hydroxychloroquine-Zinc Oxide Hybrid Nanoclusters as Synergistic Antiplasmodial Agents.
articles.autores: Rani S, Kumar B, … Manuja A (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background: The increasing emergence of antimalarial drug resistance and safety concerns associated with conventional therapies necessitates the development of improved compounds. In this study, we report the synthesis of hydroxychloroquine-zinc oxide hybrid nanoclusters (HCQ-ZnONPs) by integrating a bioactive organic ligand (hydroxychloroquine) with a bioactive metal oxide nanocluster (ZnONPs). Methods: Structural and physicochemical characterization was performed using proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR), fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), mass spectrometry, X-ray diffraction (XRD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (EDAX), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and zeta potential.
