Although DS is guideline-endorsed and biologically well-defined, scalable implementation is limited by reader-dependent variability and lack of standardized automation.
METHODS: We developed Cytoreader-Fusion, a transparent, ensemble-based AI system for automated slide-level DS classification within HPV-based screening workflows that produces well-calibrated probabilistic outputs. The model was trained on 1919 cases and evaluated under blinded honest-broker oversight on 9006 cases across four independent cohorts, including a fully independent post-lock external validation cohort (EXVC; n=4996). All preprocessing steps, aggregation rules, and decision parameters were prespecified and irreversibly locked prior to validation. Performance was evaluated against independently ascertained histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse (CIN 3+) (or anal intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse [AIN 3+]) end points rather than cytologic concordance. A single unified classifier was applied across both ThinPrep and SurePath preparations without platform-specific retraining.
RESULTS: Cytoreader-Fusion demonstrated stable and reproducible slide-level classification across imaging variability, preparation platforms, and clinical settings. Across blinded screening and referral cohorts, sensitivity and specificity were higher than atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse (ASC-US+) Papanicolaou (Pap) cytology in HPV-based screening populations and comparable to or exceeded manual DS interpretation. In the fully independent post-lock cohort (n=4996), the locked system achieved a sensitivity of 88.3% (90% UI, 85.3%-91.3%) and a specificity of 54.4% (90% UI, 52.9%-55.9%) for detection of CIN 3+, without any model retraining, threshold tuning, or configuration adjustment after lock. Operating characteristics remained consistent across cohorts and preparation platforms.
CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a high-stringency validation framework for clinically deployable artificial intelligence in population-based cancer screening. By combining prespecified algorithm locking, independent blinded evaluation under honest-broker supervision, end point-based validation against histologically confirmed disease, and cross-platform generalization, Cytoreader-Fusion demonstrates robust and scalable automation of DS triage within HPV-based screening programs. (Funded by the U.S. National Cancer Institute and others.).

articles.titulo: Integrating Host Transcriptomics and Metagenomics in the Periparturient Dairy Cow: From Molecular Signatures to Host-Microbiome Interfaces.
articles.autores: Ma Q, Tharwat M, … Khan MZ (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The periparturient or transition period-roughly three weeks before to three weeks after calving-compresses the most severe metabolic, endocrine and immunological demands of the production cycle into a few weeks and accounts for most clinical disease and involuntary culling in dairy herds. Conventional surveillance relies on downstream indicators-non-esterified fatty acids, β-hydroxybutyrate, calcium and acute-phase proteins-that document failed adaptation without resolving its regulatory origins. Two omics platforms now close that gap. Transcriptomics shows that the liver, adipose tissue, mammary gland, endometrium, rumen epithelium and circulating leukocytes each execute a distinct, temporally ordered program organized around lipid mobilization, gluconeogenesis, endoplasmic reticulum stress, redox defense and inflammatory resolution, layered over a regulatory tier of non-coding RNAs. Metagenomics shows in parallel that rumen, hindgut, uterine, vaginal, teat-apex and colostrum communities are restructured by parturition and by the dietary shift into lactation, with reproducible dysbiotic signatures accompanying ketosis, fatty liver, metritis, endometritis and intramammary infection. Critically, the two layers are mechanistically coupled: microbial short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, purine derivatives and amino acids reprogram hepatic and immune cell transcription, while host lipolysis, inflammation and mineral demand reshape community structure. This review synthesizes both groups of literature within a single framework, formalizes five host-microbiome interfaces supported by paired measurements and identifies the biomarker, nutritional and genetic-selection opportunities that emerge only when host and microbial evidence are read together.

articles.titulo: Microbial Dysbiosis, Infection, and Immunometabolic Signaling in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (Formerly PCOS).
articles.autores: Nevins A, Stansbury N, … Zhong G (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), recently proposed as a new name for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a heterogeneous endocrine-metabolic disorder characterized by hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and variable ovarian morphology. Low-grade inflammation is common, but its initiating and sustaining factors differ among phenotypes. Microbial communities have emerged as potential modifiers of this inflammatory and metabolic environment. Human studies generally identify differences in gut microbial community structure between affected and unaffected women, although no universal taxonomic signature has been reproduced across regions, phenotypes, or analytic platforms. Mechanistic studies implicate altered intestinal barrier signaling, microbial metabolites, bile acid-interleukin-22 pathways, and immune-cell polarization; however, several influential pathways remain supported principally by animal models. Evidence for lower genital tract dysbiosis is more limited, and apparent associations may reflect hormonal state, menstrual irregularity, adiposity, medications, sexual exposures, or sampling methods. Evidence that specific infections cause PMOS/PCOS is sparse and inconsistent. Small serologic studies involving Chlamydia species and Helicobacter pylori do not establish temporality or causality. This review distinguishes dysbiosis from infection, evaluates human and experimental evidence, and proposes a bidirectional microbial-immune-metabolic-ovarian framework. A focused hypothesis involving interleukin-12-STAT4 signaling is also examined because it provides a specific, testable framework linking microbial or sterile inflammatory signaling to ovarian dysfunction. STAT4 can promote inflammatory T-helper-1 programs and granulosa-cell apoptosis in non-PCOS models, while estrogen can enhance STAT4 activation; nevertheless, direct human PMOS/PCOS evidence is currently absent, and the proposed pathway should not be interpreted as an established disease mechanism. Future studies require deep phenotyping, longitudinal multi-omics, compartment-specific sampling, standardized analysis, and mechanistic validation before microbiome-directed or immune-directed interventions can enter clinical care.

articles.titulo: Itaconate-based hydrogels for immunomodulation and infection control: design strategies, biomedical applications, and translational challenges.
articles.autores: Wang M, Wang J, … Yang H (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Itaconate is a bioactive immunometabolite with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. Its unsaturated dicarboxylic structure allows for versatile polymerization and chemical functionalization. These characteristics make it a promising building block for bioactive hydrogels. However, current research on itaconate-based hydrogels is fragmented across immunology, polymer chemistry, and biomedical engineering, with a lack of a unified design framework. In this review, we summarize the biological properties of itaconate and its derivatives relevant to biomaterial design, including immunomodulatory effects and antimicrobial activity. We categorize itaconate-based hydrogels into two main strategies: those directly fabricated from itaconate or its analogues, and those loaded with itaconate or itaconate derivatives such as 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI) and dimethyl itaconate (DMI). We explore the relationships between composition, crosslinking chemistry, responsiveness, biological functions, and therapeutic applications in drug delivery, tissue repair, inflammatory diseases, and anti-infective therapy. We also highlight critical limitations, including insufficient structure-function comparisons, overreliance on small-animal models, limited mechanistic validation, and challenges in manufacturing, stability, biosafety, and clinical translation. This review presents a conceptual framework for the rational design of itaconate-based hydrogels and outlines key priorities for advancing these materials toward clinical translation as bioactive and immunomodulatory hydrogel platforms.

articles.titulo: NLRC3 deficiency exacerbates high-fat diet-induced enteric nervous system injury and colonic motility dysfunction in mice via activating NF-κB signaling pathway.
articles.autores: Wang Y, Li Y, … Li YQ (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: A high-fat diet (HFD) induces low-grade intestinal inflammation, thereby causing structural and functional impairments of the enteric nervous system (ENS). Nucleotide oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor (NLR) containing a caspase activation and recruitment domain 3 (NLRC3) participates in key pathophysiological processes related to inflammation, immunity, and proliferative diseases. However, the function of NLRC3 within the ENS remains to be clarified. This investigation was designed to characterize NLRC3 expression and distribution within the ENS and to elucidate its mechanism in modulating ENS injury. An HFD-induced low-grade colonic inflammation model was established in NLRC3 gene knockout (Nlrc3-/-) mice and wild-type (WT) C57BL/6J mice. The influence of NLRC3 on ENS architecture and motor function was assessed using morphological evaluation, molecular biological assays, and colonic motility analyses. The findings demonstrated that NLRC3 was primarily distributed within the cytoplasm of ENS neurons in mice, with HFD decreasing NLRC3 expression in enteric neurons. Relative to WT mice, HFD-treated Nlrc3-/- mice developed more pronounced ENS injury, characterized by enteric glial cells proliferation and activation, enteric neuronal loss accompanied by structural disruption, and a further delay in colonic transit function. NLRC3 deficiency exacerbated HFD-induced ENS injury and enteric neuronal apoptosis via nuclear factor-κB signaling pathway activation. These observations establish NLRC3 as a key negative regulator of neuroinflammatory responses in the ENS. As a negative regulatory pattern recognition receptor that links innate immunity with ENS signaling, NLRC3 may represent a promising therapeutic target.

articles.titulo: Post-acute infection: before we forget it again.
articles.autores: Madsen HB, Desler C
articles.resumo_original: Long COVID did not invent the post-acute phase of infection; it made it impossible to ignore. Acute infections are still often framed as time-limited events that end in recovery, deterioration or death, but this view fails to capture patients who remain biologically and clinically unwell after the acute infection has passed. The problem extends beyond SARS-CoV-2. Post-acute morbidity has been described after influenza, Epstein-Barr virus infection, Q fever, sepsis, and other infections, yet definitions, coding systems, and clinical pathways remain fragmented. We argue that post-acute infection should not be organized only by the initiating pathogen. Such pathogen-centric labels may be clinically tidy, but they risk producing heterogeneous cohorts, diluted biomarker signals, and disease-specific silos that obscure shared mechanisms of incomplete recovery. Instead, the field needs a second axis: the host-recovery state. Persistent inflammation, immune remodelling, loss of tolerance, antigenic stimulation, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial impairment, and tissue injury may represent overlapping immunometabolic failure modes across infections. Defining these states over time could help transform post-acute infection from a residual clinical label into a mechanism-informed framework for research, biomarkers, and care.

articles.titulo: A modular in vitro multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of high-value vidarabine 5'-monophosphate from adenosine.
articles.autores: Su W, Zhang X, … Liu Y (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Nucleoside analogues such as vidarabine (Ara-A) are vital therapeutics but are often limited by poor pharmacokinetics. Its phosphorylated form, vidarabine 5'-monophosphate (Ara-AMP), offers improved solubility and is used as a clinical alternative, although it can be dephosphorylated to Ara-A in vivo. Here, we report a modular multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of Ara-AMP directly from adenosine. The cascade integrates three functional modules: a core module (PNP, PPM, and RpiA) for the conversion of adenosine to Ara-A, a driver module (dNKδ20) for the selective phosphorylation of Ara-A to Ara-AMP, and a support module (PPK) for ATP regeneration from low-cost ADP and polyphosphate. The use of dNKδ20, a mutant deoxyribonucleoside kinase with high selectivity for Ara-A over adenosine, is critical for minimizing the formation of AMP byproduct, which would otherwise complicate downstream processing. Under optimized conditions, the cascade achieved an 80.2% conversion of 1 mM adenosine to Ara-AMP in 4 h using 0.05 mM ADP. The modular design was also applicable to guanosine and inosine, affording the corresponding arabinosyl nucleotides, albeit with lower yields. This work establishes a sustainable biocatalytic platform for nucleoside analogues, exemplifying how enzyme promiscuity, thermodynamic driving, and cofactor recycling enable green pharmaceutical manufacturing.

articles.titulo: Microtubules coordinate cellularization in a coenocytic relative of animals.
articles.autores: Araújo M, Olivetta M, … Dudin O (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cellularization is the coordinated division of a multinucleate cell into many cells, a common life cycle transition across eukaryotes. In the best-studied model of this process, Drosophila melanogaster, cellularization requires actin and microtubule networks, as well as membrane vesicle delivery to drive the synchronous invagination of plasma membrane furrows. To identify unifying principles, we investigate cellularization in the ichthyosporean Sphaeroforma arctica, a close relative of animals with a multinucleate life cycle stage. Using live-cell imaging, ultrastructure expansion microscopy, and volume electron microscopy, we define the membrane, microtubule, and actin dynamics that accompany cellularization. Using pharmacological inhibitors and centrifugation, we show that the microtubule network positions nuclei evenly at the cortex, thereby specifying furrow positioning. Disrupting microtubules perturbed nuclear position, furrow spacing, and the efficiency of furrow ingression, leading eventually to cells of variable size and nuclear content. Our findings indicate that the microtubule network sets the spatial framework within which actomyosin and membrane delivery drive cellularization and establish S. arctica as a tractable model for comparative studies of this eukaryotic life cycle strategy.

articles.titulo: 3D Reconstruction of Nanoparticle Distribution in Tumor Spheroids With Volume Electron Microscopy.
articles.autores: Bottone D, Gerken LRH, … Herrmann IK (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Spatially resolved characterization of nanomaterial (NM) distribution within cellular ultrastructure is essential for understanding NM fate and activity in biological systems. Volume electron microscopy (vEM) is uniquely positioned to address this challenge, yet fully documented quantitative pipelines that simultaneously segment NMs and cellular structures remain scarce. Here, an end-to-end analytical pipeline is presented based on the example of serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBF-SEM) data of tumor spheroids containing nanoparticles (NPs). A hybrid segmentation strategy is adopted, comprising a fine-tuned Cellpose-SAM model for cells and nuclei, and an empirical Bayes approach for AuNPs. The fine-tuned model outperforms both the pre-trained baseline and the benchmark experiments in Amira, and shows good generalization to 2D EM datasets of varying sample types, suggesting potential as a general-purpose segmentation model for electron microscopy. Full 3D reconstruction of NP distributions reveals preferential clustering in the perinuclear region, with a median nucleus-to-NP distance of 2.57 μ m  and NM uptake spanning several orders of magnitude across cells. Furthermore, morphological analysis of segmented cells and nuclei using 3D shape descriptors and local curvature metrics provides quantitative access to features inaccessible from single sections. Together, these results establish a reproducible, open framework for the joint quantitative analysis of NM distribution and cellular morphology in vEM data.

articles.titulo: Engineering zero thermal expansion over a wide temperature range in PbTiO3-based ferroelectrics.
articles.autores: Pan Z, Ye M, … Long Y (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Thermal expansion mismatches in precision optics, aerospace, and electronics can lead to delamination and fatigue, driving urgent demand for zero thermal expansion (ZTE) materials. At present, the majority of single-phase ZTE materials only function effectively below 500 K, limiting potential applications in many critical fields. Herein, we employ high-pressure and high-temperature synthesis to develop (1 - x)PbTiO3-xBi(Cu3/4W1/4)O3 perovskite ferroelectrics, utilizing spontaneous volume ferroelectrostriction to achieve an ultrawide ZTE regime from 300 to 725 K. In situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction tracks the lattice contraction and phase stability, while transmission electron microscopy provides insights into atomic-scale A/B-site cation displacements and tetragonal distortions. First-principles calculations reveal that polar ferroelectric-active Bi3+, Cu2+, and W6+ ions synergistically reorganize electron density to reinforce ferroelectric distortion, while Cu-derived van Hove singularities near the Fermi level dominate the density of states and govern the elastic anomalies linked to the ultrawide ZTE behaviors. This study extends the scope of high-temperature ZTE materials and establishes a ferroelectric-active ion-doping strategy to engineer thermal expansion.

articles.titulo: Inositol hexakisphosphate kinase 1 regulates polyphosphate synthesis by maintaining V-ATPase-dependent secretory granule acidification.
articles.autores: Mallick M, Bhandari R
articles.resumo_original: Polyphosphate (polyP), a linear polymer of orthophosphate residues, is enriched in secretory granules in specialised mammalian cell types including platelets and mast cells. Although polyP released during activation and degranulation of these cells has been shown to promote blood clotting and inflammation, little is known about the mechanisms governing polyP synthesis in these granules. In mice, the loss of IP6K1, an enzyme that catalyses the production of 5-InsP7, has been shown to result in depletion of platelet polyP and impaired hemostasis. Here, we use the rat mast cell line RBL-2H3 as a model to study the regulation of polyP synthesis in secretory granules. By monitoring real-time polyP synthesis in isolated mast cell granules, we demonstrate that ATP is the substrate fuelling granule polyP production. By the use of inhibitors, we show that accumulation of polyP in granules requires an intact transmembrane proton gradient maintained by vacuolar H+ATPase (V-ATPase). In RBL-2H3 cells, depletion of IP6K1 led to a substantial reduction in cellular polyP levels and defective accumulation of polyP, serotonin, and tryptase inside granules. Cells with reduced IP6K1 showed a profound loss of granule acidification, correlating with downregulated levels of V1 subunits of V-ATPase. Adding back active or catalytically inactive IP6K1 rescued the expression of V-ATPase V1 subunits, reversed granule deacidification, and restored polyP levels in IP6K1-depleted cells. Together, these data unveil a role for IP6K1 in maintaining granule pH and thereby supporting polyP synthesis in mammals.

articles.titulo: Microstructure-driven opacity of semi-permeable membranes in push-pull osmotic tablets and its impact on manufacturability and drug release.
articles.autores: Lee HD, Punia A, … Lallow E (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Push-pull osmotic pump tablets provide controlled, zero-order drug release through water diffusion across a semi-permeable membrane and extrusion of the drug in the active layer through a laser-drilled orifice. The membranes must be mechanically robust to channel the internal osmotic pressure towards drug extrusion. The study reports an instance in which the solvent coating produced opaque cellulose acetate/PEG3350 semi-permeable membranes. This reduced the visual contrast between the push and pull layers-creating a potential risk for accurate laser drilling-and led to incomplete dissolution of investigational drug MK-8189 after 24 h. Scanning electron microscopy, light microscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, nanoindentation, x-ray micro-computed tomography, and dissolution testing were used to identify the origin and impact of the opacity. Results showed that opacity was driven by coating-induced membrane porosity, rather than phase separation. Although both presentations retained the zero-order release kinetics, the opaque membranes were more porous and mechanically weaker-exhibiting a three-fold increase in the number of pores, a statistically significant increase in pore size distribution, and a 26% reduction Young's Modulus than the transparent membranes. During dissolution, the softer opaque membranes deformed substantially, increasing internal tablet volume and reducing the fraction of swelling capacity available to drive the drug extrusion. Consequently, opaque tablets plateaued at ∼85% drug release, whereas transparent tablets achieved complete release. By understanding the edges of failure for the solvent coating process, optimization of the air-to-spray ratio, product temperature, and pattern air pressure eliminated the microstructural porosity.

articles.titulo: Amyloid-mediated RNA uptake by sperm for embryonic delivery.
articles.autores: Mallen WS, Zabello N, … Fitzpatrick AWP (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Seminal fluid (SF) RNA is essential for embryonic development, but the mechanism by which extracellular RNA is transferred from SF to sperm remains unclear. Here, we identify a role for functional amyloid fibrils in SF that bind and traffic RNA to mammalian sperm and, upon fertilization, to the zygote. We show that highly cationic peptides in SF phase separate with RNA to form amyloid fibrils. Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET), volume electron microscopy (volume EM), and fluorescence live-cell imaging reveal that these amyloid fibrils are internalized by mammalian sperm. Furthermore, biophysical and in vitro fertilization (IVF) experiments show that amyloid-bound RNA reaches the zygote, where molecular chaperones can control RNA dissociation from amyloid fibrils. Our work uncovers a mechanism for RNA trafficking from SF to the zygote, establishing amyloid fibrils as potential tools for RNA delivery during fertilization.

articles.titulo: Characterization and anticancer activity of green-synthesized and highly stable ginger-derived silver nanoparticles: In vitro and in vivo studies.
articles.autores: Elghaznawy MM, El Sadda RR, Saad EA
articles.resumo_original: Ginger (Zingiber officinale) is a common spice with therapeutic potential due to its bioactive compounds and was used for the green synthesis of ginger-derived silver nanoparticles (G-AgNPs). The cytotoxic, antioxidant, and pro-apoptotic effects of the synthesized G-AgNPs were evaluated against HepG-2, MCF-7, and WI-38 cell lines. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis identified 36 phytochemicals, with major components including α-zingiberene (37.88%), β-sesquiphellandrene (15.65%), 6-gingerol (10.68%), α-farnesene (8.04%), β-bisabolene (7.83%), α-curcumene (6.96%), 8-gingerol (0.96%), and 6-shogaol (0.95%). Characterization of G-AgNPs using ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), zeta-potential analysis (- 46.17 ± 1.42 mV), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed spherical nanoparticles with an average diameter of 10.44 nm. Cytotoxicity assays demonstrated greater inhibition of HepG-2 and MCF-7 cell viability than of WI-38 cells, with IC₅₀ values of 1.20 ± 0.03 µM (4.51 ± 0.11 µg/mL) and 1.49 ± 0.05 µM (5.60 ± 0.19 µg/mL), respectively, compared with 2.49 ± 0.07 µM for WI-38 cells. Treatment with G-AgNPs significantly increased caspase-3-associated protein levels in both HepG-2 (13.81 ± 0.35 ng/mg protein) and MCF-7 (42.83 ± 1.47 ng/mg protein), and decreased Bcl-2 expression (HepG-2: 2.12 ± 0.14 ng/mg protein; MCF-7: 3.17 ± 0.03 ng/mg protein). However, given the known deficiency of functional caspase-3 in MCF-7 cells, the observed increase likely reflects caspase-3-immunoreactive protein rather than active enzyme. Antioxidant evaluation demonstrated free radical scavenging activity (IC₅₀ = 28.96 µg/mL), comparable to ascorbic acid (IC₅₀ = 14.03 µg/mL), along with significant CT- DNA intercalation. In vivo, treatment of Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC)-bearing mice with G-AgNPs significantly reduced abdominal circumference, ascitic fluid volume, and viable tumor cell counts while increasing the percentage increase in lifespan by 93.3%. G-AgNPs also improved liver and kidney function, increased hepatic GSH, SOD, TAC, and catalase levels relative to untreated EAC-bearing mice, reduced oxidative stress markers (MDA and NO), and ameliorated liver histopathological alterations, with fewer adverse effects than cisplatin. The findings indicate that G-AgNPs possess potential anticancer activity and preliminary differential cytotoxicity toward HepG2 cells compared with non-cancerous cells. Further toxicological and in vivo investigations are required to establish their safety and therapeutic applicability.

articles.titulo: Lighting Up upon Phosphate Binding: Supramolecular Assembly of Ir(III) Complexes for Luminescent Sensing and Molecular Logic Gate.
articles.autores: Ghosh R, Rashid A, … Ghosh P (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Inorganic phosphates and polyphosphates are vital to biological function, and their dysregulation is linked to metabolic and renal disorders, driving the need for selective, sensitive, and reversible luminescent probes for their detection. Here, we report three bis-heteroleptic Ir(III) complexes (IC1-IC3) bearing imidazole-functionalized ancillary ligands that show selective "switch-on" emission toward phosphate (H2PO4-) and pyrophosphate (HP2O73-) over competing anions, driven by C-H···O hydrogen bonding between imidazole donors and phosphate oxygens. Variable-temperature studies (80-300 K) reveal long-lived phosphorescence (τ = 1.4 μs at 80 K) governed by restricted intramolecular motion and a large singlet-triplet gap. Emission analysis shows mixed 3MLCT character for IC1/IC2, while nitro-substituted IC3 displays combined 3MLCT/3LLCT character. The interaction of IC1 with H2PO4- gives a 1:2 binding stoichiometry (K = 8.0 × 105 M-1) and detection limits of 35.4 nM and 16.3 nM for H2PO4- and HP2O73-, respectively. NMR and DLS studies indicate that phosphate binding triggers hydrogen-bond-mediated supramolecular aggregation, rigidifying the excited state and enhancing emission, while Zn2+ reversibly quenches this response, enabling switch-on/switch-off behavior applicable to molecular logic gate. Phosphate binding extends IC1's excited-state lifetime from 91.68 to 357.66 ns. These Ir(III) complexes thus emerge as a tunable platform for selective, reversible phosphate sensing.

articles.titulo: Depth-Aware Machine Learning for 3D Reconstruction of Fibrous Porous Electrodes by FIB-SEM Tomography.
articles.autores: Bozal-Ginesta C, Bissattini Alessi C, … Battaglia C (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Quantitative three-dimensional reconstruction of porous polymers with sub-micrometer feature sizes is central to understanding and designing electrochemical interfaces and membranes. However, focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy tomography combined with conventional segmentation techniques cannot readily reconstruct complex disordered morphologies such as fibers. Standard segmentation workflows misclassify out-of-plane material as in-plane material, distorting the reconstructed pore network, fiber connectivity, and interface area. Here, we introduce an annotation-free, depth-aware machine-learning framework that combines monocular depth estimation, trained on macroscale images, with unsupervised clustering to separate in-plane polymer cross-sections from subsurface contributions in serial FIB-SEM tomography images. Applied to copper-coated electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) fiber mats, the approach produces 3D reconstructions that preserve fibrous morphology more faithfully than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation. Quantitative validation against capillary flow porometry, pycnometry, and high-resolution wide-angle X-ray computed tomography demonstrates improved agreement across pore cross-section diameter, fiber volume ratio, and Cu depth decrease metrics. This work establishes depth-aware segmentation as a transferable strategy from real-scale to nanoscale imaging, requiring no labeled training data and enabling accurate 3D segmentation and reconstruction from SEM images. This approach opens a path toward more reliable structure-property relationships in disordered porous polymer materials.

articles.titulo: Biomass-derived branched polyamine-functionalized chitosan/sodium alginate aerogels for efficient indoor low-concentration HCHO capture under high humidity.
articles.autores: Wu S, Wang D, … Hu K (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Indoor low-concentration formaldehyde (HCHO) remains a health concern, while many amine-functionalized adsorbents show reduced performance at high relative humidity (RH). Herein, chitosan/sodium alginate aerogels functionalized with cyanuric chloride (CYC) and tetraethylenepentamine (TEPA) were developed for HCHO capture. The unmodified aerogel was designated CSA. CSCPA-1, CSCPA-2, and CSCPA-3 were prepared at CSA: CYC: TEPA feed mass ratios of 5:1.8:2.8, 5:4.6:7.1, and 5:7.4:11.4, respectively. Scanning electron microscopy and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller analyses showed that polyamine functionalization altered the pore-wall morphology and porous structure, with CSCPA-2 retaining a relatively open and intact pore architecture and exhibiting the largest specific surface area and pore volume among the modified samples. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy supported the incorporation of triazine- and polyamine-containing functionalities, while XPS further indicated enrichment of nitrogen-containing chemical environments. At an initial HCHO concentration of 0.6 mg·m-3 and 25 °C, CSCPA-2 achieved removal efficiencies of 89%, 92%, 98%, and 93% at 30%, 50%, 70%, and 90% RH, respectively. At 70% RH, its adsorption capacity reached 0.264 ± 0.017 mg·g-1 (n = 3), approximately 3.5-fold that of pristine CSA. HCHO adsorption kinetics of the CSCPA aerogels were better described by the pseudo-second-order model, while spectroscopic changes before and after adsorption supported the involvement of amine-containing sites in HCHO capture. In the fourth adsorption-regeneration cycle, CSCPA-2 retained 95.98% removal efficiency and 0.2286 ± 0.0023 mg·g-1 adsorption capacity. These results highlight its potential for indoor low-concentration HCHO removal and provide a facile strategy for designing humidity-tolerant biomass-derived adsorbents.

articles.titulo: Reduced-dose alternate-day oral iron supplementation in women with iron deficiency: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.autores: Valerii MC, Dussias NK, … Spisni E (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
PURPOSE: Oral iron supplementation is frequently limited by gastrointestinal side effects and reduced absorption associated with hepcidin-mediated regulation. This randomized, parallel-group, active-controlled study evaluated whether a reduced-dose alternate-day oral iron supplementation strategy could improve iron status in women with iron deficiency.
METHODS: Sixty-six iron-deficient women of reproductive age (18-50 years; serum ferritin < 30 ng/mL) were randomized to receive, for 42 days, either micronized, dispersible ferric pyrophosphate providing 21 mg of elemental iron every 48 h combined with a daily gut microbiota modulator, or sucrosomial ferric pyrophosphate providing 30 mg of elemental iron per day. The primary endpoint was serum ferritin, while secondary endpoints included serum iron, transferrin, transferrin saturation (TSAT), total iron-binding capacity (TIBC), hemoglobin, and red blood cell count.
RESULTS: Serum ferritin increased significantly over time in both groups (p < 0.001), with no significant differences between treatments. Comparable improvements were observed for serum iron, transferrin, TSAT, and TIBC, while hemoglobin remained stable throughout the study. Both interventions were generally well tolerated, with only mild transient gastrointestinal adverse events and no clinically relevant changes in inflammatory markers.
CONCLUSION: A reduced-dose alternate-day oral iron supplementation strategy achieved improvements in iron status comparable to standard daily supplementation despite lower cumulative iron exposure. These findings support the potential clinical relevance of physiologically informed low-dose iron supplementation strategies in women with iron deficiency.

articles.titulo: Incorporation of Calcium Polyphosphate Sub-Microparticles in Commercial Toothpastes and Their Effects on Dental Enamel.
articles.autores: da Silva JA, de Jesus Gomes L, … Lima DANL (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
UNLABELLED: Dental bleaching with 35% hydrogen peroxide (HP) can cause deleterious effects on the mineral content of enamel. In this regard, remineralizing submicroparticles of calcium polyphosphate (CaPP) have been investigated for their ability to deposit calcium ions into enamel's hydroxyapatite. Thus, this study aimed to evaluate the effects of commercial toothpastes with or without the addition of CaPP submicroparticles after in-office bleaching treatment with 35% HP regarding color (ΔE, ΔE00 and WID), microhardness (KHN), and surface roughness (Ra).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Eighty bovine incisors were randomly divided into eight groups (n = 10): NC (negative control); HP (Whiteness HP 35%-FGM); HP + CT12 (HP + Colgate Total 12); HP + CMP (HP + Colgate Máxima Proteção Anticáries); HP + CPA (HP + Colgate Sensitive Pró-Alívio); HP + SRP (HP + Sensodyne Repair and Protect); HP + CT12 + CaPP (HP + Colgate Total 12 with 1% CaPP); HP + CMP + 1% CaPP (HP + Colgate Máxima Proteção Anticáries with 1% CaPP). All samples were subjected to the mechanical brushing protocol with 825 cycles and kept in artificial saliva with daily exchanges. ΔE, ΔE00, and WID were analyzed through generalized linear models fitted for the group effect. KHN and Ra were analyzed through mixed linear models for repeated measures over time. All analysis was performed in R* software at the 5% significance level.
RESULTS: Color variation (ΔE and ΔE00) was higher in the HP + SRP group compared to NC and HP (p < 0.0001). At T1, the NC group had a lower WID than other groups (p < 0.0001). Surface microhardness (KHN) analyses showed a significant group-time interaction (p = 0.04). At T1, the HP + CPA and HP + CT12 + 1% CaPP groups showed significantly higher median KHN values than the NC, HP, HP + CT12, and HP + CMP + 1% CaPP groups (p < 0.05). Surface roughness (Ra) increased significantly after the first bleaching session, regardless of the experimental group (p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: The whitening effectiveness of 35% HP was maintained across the evaluated toothpaste formulations. Colgate Total 12 supplemented with 1% CaPP resulted in higher enamel microhardness than the corresponding formulation without CaPP, whereas no significant differences among the experimental groups were observed for surface roughness.

articles.titulo: Liquid Phase Backscattered Scanning Electron Microscopy of Bacillus subtilis Spores.
articles.autores: Bromley J, Pedrazo-Tardajos A, … Kim JS (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Backscattered electron scanning electron microscopy (BSE-SEM) provides compositional image contrast but has found limited application to biological samples due to the low atomic number difference between constituent elements, the thickness of the surrounding environment, and the need for complex sample preparation. Previous graphene-encapsulation SEM studies have demonstrated imaging of hydrated bacteria, principally to preserve or observe bacterial morphology. Here, we establish liquid phase BSE-SEM (LPBSEM) as a depth-sensitive, label-free approach for visualizing subsurface architecture in intact hydrated bacteria and Bacillus subtilis spores. This approach does not require staining and enables high-contrast visualization of subcellular structures in hydrated samples. Internal structural layers within B. subtilis spores have been observed similar to those visualized with conventional thin-section transmission electron microscopy but without the need for sample preparation that potentially compromises sample integrity. We further investigate the influence of beam energy on the interaction volume depth and image contrast and propose optimal conditions for subsurface visualization. Monte Carlo simulations were used to assess whether the observed contrast trends are consistent with expected backscatter distributions and provide a physical framework for interpretation and understanding of BSE generation from hydrated, low atomic number specimens.

articles.titulo: Epithelial Barrier-Injury Transcriptomic Stratification Across Human IBD Mucosal Cohorts.
articles.autores: Zheng H, Bu W, Zhuang X
articles.resumo_original: Public mucosal transcriptomic datasets provide an opportunity to examine whether experimental epithelial barrier biology is reflected in human inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) endpoints. We constructed a prespecified barrier-injury transcriptomic score from an inositol polyphosphate multikinase-histone deacetylase 3-matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) barrier-biology gene set and epithelial junctional genes, then evaluated it across 10 public IBD mucosal transcriptomic cohorts (2172 scored biopsies) and an independent prospective adult cohort (GSE193677; 1162 participants). Adult cohorts were analyzed for mucosal healing, clinical remission, or treatment response; pediatric and early onset cohorts were analyzed separately. In UNIFI (GSE206285), a higher baseline score was inversely associated with week 8 mucosal healing (odds ratio [OR]: 0.56, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.45-0.71, p < 0.001). In GSE193677, the score was associated with IBD compared with control status (OR: 1.71, 95% CI: 1.45-2.02) and with endoscopic and histologic activity. The association was directionally consistent across biopsy-selection analyses and exceeded expression- and variance-matched random-gene estimates (empirical p = 0.034), while MMP and inflammatory comparators were at least as strong. Single-cell data localized the MMP module predominantly to stromal cells. These findings support retrospective transcriptomic stratification of mucosal injury states and define a barrier biology-motivated bulk mucosal readout shaped by stromal inflammatory remodeling in human tissue.

articles.titulo: Polyphosphate Copper Nanospheres Drive Mitochondrial Metabolic Reprogramming via Calcium Phase Separation for Self-Sensitizing Cuproptosis.
articles.autores: Wang J, Zhao X, … Wei W (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Precise spatiotemporal control of intracellular Ca2+ signaling remains a major bottleneck in reversing tumor glycolytic dominance and reactivating mitochondrial therapies. To overcome this limitation, we developed a polyphosphate (polyP)-engineered nanoplatform that exploits liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) to drive calcium-mediated metabolic reprogramming. We discovered that FITC-polyP coacervates with Ca2+ to form biomolecular condensates that function as localized Ca2+ signaling microdomains. By selectively activating key mitochondrial enzymes, these microdomains shift tumor cells toward a mitochondria-dependent metabolic phenotype. Crucially, disturbing condensate formation via Ca2+ chelation or enzymatic degradation prevents this transition, confirming polyP/Ca2+ condensates as the indispensable master regulator of mitochondrial metabolic activation. Sustained mitochondrial reactivation creates a primed cellular state that sensitizes tumor cells to cuproptosis. This work establishes a resourceful self-sensitizing nanoplatform that utilizes polyP-induced phase separation to precisely reprogram tumor metabolism and activate cuproptosis, highlighting polyP-induced LLPS as a novel strategy for targeted cancer therapy.

articles.titulo: Nanoscale Characterization of Microscopically Layered Bone in the Russian Sturgeon Pectoral Fin Spine: A 3D FIB-SEM Study.
articles.autores: Marroquín-Arroyave E, Milgram J
articles.resumo_original: Dermal bone, the earliest known form of bone, develops without a cartilage precursor and persists in extant fish species. The pectoral fin spine (PFS) is a dermal bone located at the leading edge of the pectoral fin of sturgeons, where it is exposed to loading associated with locomotion. The peripheral region and dermal osteons of the PFS both appear layered at lower magnification; however, collagen organization in load-bearing fish skeletal elements remains incompletely characterized at the nanoscale. The aim of this study is to characterize the 3D nanostructure of the layered peripheral and osteonal bone forming the PFS in Russian sturgeons using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM). In the dermal osteons, bone forms concentric layers around a central canal at lower magnification, and at the nanoscale, the calcified collagen fibrils within these layers have preferential orientations that change in a clockwise-anticlockwise fanning pattern, consistent with lamellar bone. In contrast, the examined peripheral bone, which also appears layered at low magnification, is composed mainly of unidirectional calcified collagen fibrils aligned with the long axis of the PFS. Within the examined peripheral volumes, no comparable nanoscale lamellar pattern was detected, and the predominant fibril organization was consistent with parallel-fibered bone. Groups of voids associated with unidentified fibrillar material were also observed in the examined peripheral volumes; the voids were oriented approximately normal to the long axis of the PFS. We conclude that regions appearing layered at lower magnification can differ markedly at the nanoscale, and that the lamellar organization seen in dermal osteons raises questions about its evolutionary origin.

articles.titulo: Bromide Sequestration Using a Low-Cost Hybrid Composite of Calcium, Activated Carbon, Kaolin, and Starch.
articles.autores: Al-Mur BA, Jamal MT
articles.resumo_original: Bromide in source waters promotes the formation of toxic brominated disinfection byproducts during chlorination and ozonation, necessitating efficient, affordable pretreatment materials. This study developed a low-cost hybrid composite, denoted Calcium-Activated Carbon-Kaolin-Starch (CAKS) composite, from kaolin, activated carbon, a calcium precursor and starch through starch-assisted consolidation followed by calcination under nitrogen. The synthesized material was characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, nitrogen adsorption-desorption analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. CAKS exhibited a heterogeneous mesoporous structure with a Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 212.5 m2 g-1, a pore volume of 0.384 cm3 g-1, and an average pore diameter of 7.2 nm. Batch adsorption experiments showed that bromide uptake was strongly dependent on solution pH, adsorbent dosage, contact time, initial concentration, agitation speed, temperature, and the presence of competing ions. Maximum removal of approximately 97.3% was achieved at pH 5, close to the apparent point of zero charge of 5.5. Adsorption was rapid during the first 60 min and approached equilibrium after 90-120 min. The experimental adsorption capacity increased with increasing bromide concentration, reaching approximately 40.0 mg g-1 at an initial bromide concentration of 200 mg L-1. Equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir model, which yielded a model-estimated maximum adsorption capacity of 81.30 mg g-1. Kinetic data were described best by the pseudo-second-order model, although film diffusion and intraparticle diffusion also contributed to the overall uptake process. Equilibrium data indicated heterogeneous adsorption behavior, while thermodynamic analysis suggested that bromide adsorption was thermodynamically favorable under the investigated conditions. Regeneration with 0.1 M Sodium hydroxide and reuse over five adsorption-desorption cycles was also evaluated. Results were obtained under controlled laboratory conditions.

articles.titulo: Pore Structure, Fractal Dimension, and Methane Adsorption Capacity of Coals: A Case Study from the Huaibei Coalfield, China.
articles.autores: Wei Q, Chen S, … Li S (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The Huaibei Coalfield hosts abundant coalbed methane (CBM) resources, yet its heterogeneous pore structure poses challenges for efficient development. In this study, the multiscale pore structure was characterized using field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP), and N2/CO2 adsorption experiments, and fractal dimensions were quantified to reflect pore heterogeneity, and methane adsorption capacity was tested with the improved Langmuir equation. The results indicate that the coal samples are medium-rank bituminous coal, with a maximum vitrinite reflectance (R o,max) of 0.73%-0.96%. Vitrinite constitutes the major maceral component, while mineral contents remain low. FE-SEM and EDS analyses reveal highly heterogeneous pore fractures and mineral compositions. Of the total pore volume, micropores and macropores together account for approximately 90.81%, with volumes of 0.72-1.86 cm3/100 g (average of 1.24 cm3/100 g) and 0.32-4.99 cm3/100 g (average of 1.54 cm3/100 g), respectively. The specific surface area of micropores is 18.13-48.94 m2/g (average of 32.21 m2/g), which accounts for 99.55% of the total on average. In addition, the coal rank promotes micropore development, whereas the inertinite content negatively correlates with macropore volume. Methane adsorption capacity is 0.81-1 mmol/g (average of 0.92 mmol/g), which is primarily controlled by the volume and specific surface area of micropores but shows no relationship with the maceral or mineral component. Moreover, methane adsorption capacity shows positive correlations with fractal dimensions D N21 and D CO2 but a negative correlation with D N22. From a kinetic perspective, mesopores and macropores can accelerate gas transport and shorten equilibrium time. This study offered scientific support for CBM assessment and exploitation in the Huaibei Coalfield.

articles.titulo: Interfacial Engineering of Fe3O4/Biochar via CMC Bridging for Durable Lithium/Sodium-Ion Storage.
articles.autores: Li H, Yang Z, … Xia H (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The development of cost-effective and durable anode materials derived from renewable biomass is essential for practical lithium- and sodium-ion batteries (LIBs/SIBs). However, conventional strategies for integrating high-capacity metal oxides with biomass carbon often suffer from weak oxide-carbon adhesion, nanoparticle aggregation, and large volume changes during cycling. To overcome these limitations, we present an interfacial engineering approach in which carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) serves as a molecular bridge to anchor Fe3O4 nanoparticles in situ onto ginkgo branch-derived biochar (GBC). The abundant hydroxyl and carboxyl groups of CMC simultaneously guide uniform Fe3O4 nucleation and create a molecular bridge that mediates interfacial chemical interactions that facilitate charge transfer while accommodating volume strain. Structural and compositional analyses confirm the formation of CMC/Fe3O4/GBC with well-dispersed nanocrystals, a hierarchically porous architecture, and magnetic responsiveness. As an anode, CMC/Fe3O4/GBC delivers 256 mAh/g at 2000 mA/g in SIBs, substantially higher than that of bare GBC and unmodified Fe3O4/GBC. Comparable durability is observed in LIBs, where the composite retains 297 mAh/g after 2000 cycles at the same rate. Kinetic studies using cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic intermittent titration technique, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveal that CMC bridging enhances pseudocapacitive contribution and accelerates ion diffusion. Post-cycling X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy further confirm the preserved electrode integrity. These results establish a scalable interfacial modification strategy for biomass-derived magnetic composites toward durable alkali-ion storage.

articles.titulo: Antitumor Activity of a Bupleurum chinense-Derived Vesicle-like Particle Preparation in MOC1 Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Models.
articles.autores: Li S, Zhang G, … Ge W (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the antitumor activity of a Bupleurum chinense-derived extracellular vesicle-like particle (BC-EVLP) preparation in MOC1 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) models. Methods: Fresh roots were processed by differential centrifugation, filtration, ultracentrifugation, and sucrose density-gradient separation. The preparation was characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and total protein measurement. Cellular association, viability, ROS-associated fluorescence, mitochondrial membrane potential, and Annexin V-FITC/PI staining were assessed. Cell viability was also compared after exposure to equal added volumes of the preparation or pre-gradient ultracentrifugation supernatant. Female C57BL/6 mice bearing syngeneic MOC1 tumors received peritumoral treatment every 3 days for 14 days, followed by tumor histology. Results: The preparation contained nanoscale vesicle-like structures, with median and mean particle diameters of 162.0 and 191.9 nm. DiI-associated fluorescence was detected in MOC1 cells after 4 h. Treatment reduced cell viability and was associated with increased DCF fluorescence, a lower JC-1 red/green ratio, and increased Annexin V-positive fractions. The BC-EVLP preparation reduced cell viability more than the supernatant at equal added volumes, although the higher-volume supernatant treatment retained partial activity. High-dose treatment attenuated tumor growth in vivo, and representative tumor sections showed less densely cellular areas. Conclusions: The BC-EVLP preparation exhibited antitumor activity in the tested MOC1 models. The active constituents and the relative contributions of vesicular and non-vesicular components remain unresolved.

articles.titulo: Sustainable Hybrid Flame-Retardant Architectures for LDPE: Effects of Waste-Derived Cellulose, SiO2, and APP/ADA.
articles.autores: Ruiz-Martínez ARY, Cabrera-Álvarez EN, … Contreras-López D (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study evaluates the flame retardant efficiency of hybrid systems based on natural cellulose extracted from agricultural wastes (pecan nutshell and guayule), combined with azodicarbonamide (ADA), porous silicon dioxide (SiO2) scaffolds, and ammonium polyphosphate (APP), incorporated into low-density polyethylene (LDPE). The waste-derived cellulose fractions were isolated via alkaline extraction and steam explosion, yielding microfibrils that preserved native lignin fractions. Porous SiO2 particles were modified through the adsorption of ADA and APP, which in turn decorated the surface of the cellulose particles. Hybrid LDPE composites containing 20 wt% of total additives were melt-compounded and characterized. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed an early intumescent activation that promoted robust charring, achieving final char residue yields up to 9.5 wt% for the pecan nutshell composite. Horizontal UL-94 and cone calorimeter tests demonstrated the complete elimination of hazardous flaming melt-dripping across all formulated hybrid systems, accompanied by a significant reduction in the burning rate to 18.3 mm/min and a 45% reduction in PHRR for the pecan nutshell-derived compound, consistent with a protective contribution of the multifunctional particles in the condensed phase, significantly outperforming its commercial nanocellulose counterparts. Cone calorimetry highlighted a drastic flattening of the peak heat release rate (PHRR) kinetics of composites. FTIR, TEM and TGA analyses confirmed the formation of a APP-ADA-loaded SiO2 particle scaffold ("grenade-like" morphology), with combustion-residue FTIR and SEM/EDS supporting a protective contribution in the condensed phase.

articles.titulo: Syringe filter-SPE for determination of organophosphorus pesticides and atrazine in environmental water samples using Cr-MOF/ graphene nano-powder composite as sorbent.
articles.autores: Mohammed AM, Khodayari A, … Moinfar S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The efficiency of solid-phase extraction (SPE) for determining low-concentration organophosphorus pesticides and atrazine in real samples depends on the adsorbent's ability to adsorb the analyte before entering the chromatography system. MOFs can be an excellent option as adsorbents for extracting analytes because of their large specific surface area and high adsorption capacity, particularly NH2-MIL-101(Cr). The aim of this study is to enhance extraction efficiency and sensitivity in a syringe-filter solid-phase extraction (SPE) method using a novel NH2-MIL-101(Cr) composite for the extraction of several organophosphorus pesticides (OPPs) and atrazine from environmental water samples. In this study, an NH2-MIL-101(Cr)/graphene nanocomposite was synthesized for the first time and packed into a syringe filter as an adsorbent, thereby increasing the method's sensitivity. Various characterisation techniques, including fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were employed to verify the successful production of the nanocomposite. The variables influencing the extraction efficiency of NH2-MIL-101(Cr)/Graphene nano-powder-syringe filter-SPE/GC-MS, including sample volume, pH, elution solvent volume, and elution solvent type, were optimized. The findings indicated that the Cr-MOF/GNP nanocomposite exhibited enhanced adsorption efficacy and a reduced detection limit for all nine target pesticides compared with unmodified NH2-MIL-101 (Cr). The technique demonstrated a linear response range of 1.0 to 300.0 μg/L and achieved detection limits of 0.2 to 6.0 μg/L. The results demonstrated significant reproducibility, with outstanding recovery rates ranging from 83.0% to 103.0% across increasing concentrations from 15.0 to 60.0 μg/L and relative standard deviation values ranging from 3.2% to 6.3%.

articles.titulo: Upcycling Used Tyre Rubber into Carbon Adsorbents: Effect of Physical Activation on Porous Structure and Comparative Evaluation for p-Chlorophenol Removal.
articles.autores: Troca-Torrado C, Alexandre-Franco MF, … Gómez-Serrano V (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The porous architecture of carbons derived from polymeric waste is largely governed by the physical activation atmosphere. In this work, used tyre rubber (UTR) was converted into carbonaceous adsorbents by pyrolysis followed by physical activation in air, CO2 or steam. The influence of the activation route on porous structure, surface chemistry and adsorption performance was systematically investigated. The materials were characterised by N2 adsorption at -196 °C, mercury intrusion porosimetry, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), FT-IR spectroscopy and point-of-zero-charge (pHpzc) measurements. The resulting materials were evaluated for the removal of p-chlorophenol from aqueous solution and comparatively assessed against three commercial carbon materials. Steam activation proved to be the most effective treatment, increasing the BET surface area from 64 to 344 m2 g-1 and the micropore volume from 0.05 to 0.23 cm3 g-1 while generating a hierarchical micro-/mesoporous structure that significantly enhanced pore accessibility and mass transport. Among the UTR-derived carbons, the steam-activated sample exhibited the highest equilibrium p-Cp uptake and adsorption kinetics approaching those of a commercial activated carbon despite its lower specific surface area. Kinetic and equilibrium analyses demonstrated that adsorption performance depends not only on the extent of microporosity but also on pore accessibility and network connectivity, highlighting the critical role of transport mesoporosity in facilitating molecular diffusion towards adsorption sites. The adsorption results are consistent with an important contribution from accessible microporosity, while π-π interactions between p-chlorophenol and aromatic carbon domains may also contribute. These findings demonstrate that tailoring porous structure through physical activation provides an effective strategy for transforming UTR into high-performance carbon adsorbents and establishes robust processing-structure-property relationships that can guide the rational design of waste-derived carbon adsorbents.

articles.titulo: Effect of Build Orientation on the Electrical, Thermal, and Mechanical Properties of PA12 Fabricated by Selective Laser Sintering.
articles.autores: Huang L, Tu S, … Li H (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Selective laser sintering (SLS) provides a promising route for the rapid fabrication of polymeric insulating components with complex geometries. However, its layer-by-layer manufacturing process inherently introduces structural anisotropy, which may significantly affect the electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties of the printed materials. In this study, polyamide 12 (PA12) specimens fabricated by SLS at different printing orientations were systematically investigated for dielectric properties, volume resistivity, DC and AC breakdown strength, tensile properties, and thermal conductivity. Scanning electron microscopy and X-ray microscopy were further employed to characterize the microstructure and clarify the origin of the anisotropic behavior. The results show that SLS-printed PA12 exhibits pronounced orientation-dependent properties. As the printing angle increases from 0° to 90°, the volume resistivity and DC breakdown strength generally decrease. In contrast, the relative permittivity generally increases with printing angle, whereas the AC breakdown strength and dielectric loss exhibit more complex non-monotonic variations. The tensile strength and elongation at break both gradually decrease with increasing printing angle. The thermal conductivity varies only slightly across different orientations but increases overall with printing angle. Microstructural observations reveal numerous interlayer pores, incompletely sintered regions, and heterogeneous interfaces with a distinct layered distribution. These heterogeneous interlayer structures affect the transport of charge, heat, and load, thereby contributing to the anisotropic electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties of SLS-printed PA12. These findings provide a basis for optimizing the printing orientation and structural design of SLS-printed PA12 for high-voltage insulation applications.

articles.titulo: Polyphosphate-Functionalized PGMA-Grafted Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles for Selective U(VI) Removal from Aqueous Solutions.
articles.autores: Alshammari AS, Alosime EM, Basfar AA
articles.resumo_original: Uranium(VI) contamination in aquatic environments poses significant environmental and public health concerns, creating a need for efficient and selective adsorbents. In this study, polyphosphate-functionalized poly(glycidyl methacrylate)-grafted mesoporous silica nanoparticles (PP-PGMA/MSNs) were successfully synthesized and evaluated for U(VI) removal from aqueous solutions. A key novelty of this work lies in the incorporation of phosphate-rich functionalities onto PGMA-grafted MSNs prepared via ATRP, together with the systematic investigation of their effects on U(VI) adsorption equilibrium and selectivity in multi-metal systems. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) confirmed the successful incorporation of phosphate-containing functional groups onto the MSN surface. The adsorbent exhibited rapid adsorption, reaching equilibrium within 120 min, with optimum performance observed at pH 4-6. A maximum U(VI) removal efficiency of 73.81% was achieved at an initial concentration of 10 mg L-1, while the maximum adsorption capacity reached 114.94 mg g-1. Equilibrium data were well described by the Langmuir isotherm model (R2 = 0.9697), indicating predominantly monolayer adsorption on relatively homogeneous adsorption sites. Despite a substantial reduction in surface area following functionalization, the material maintained a high adsorption capacity, suggesting that uranium uptake is governed primarily by interactions at phosphate-containing active sites. Furthermore, the adsorbent exhibited preferential affinity toward U(VI) in multi-metal systems containing Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, and Pb ions, demonstrating enhanced selectivity toward uranyl species. The adsorption behavior suggests that phosphate functionalities serve as the primary binding sites through surface complexation and coordination interactions. These findings demonstrate the potential of PP-PGMA/MSNs as selective adsorbents for U(VI) removal from complex aqueous systems and environmental remediation applications.

articles.titulo: Electrospun Carbon Nanofiber-TiN Composite Interlayers for Improved Cycling Stability and Rate Capability of Lithium-Sulfur Batteries.
articles.autores: Niu C, Liu H, Chao Z
articles.resumo_original: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries offer a high theoretical energy density of 2600 Wh·kg-1 and a theoretical specific capacity of 1675 mAh·g-1; however, their practical application is severely hindered by the shuttle effect of soluble lithium polysulfides, the intrinsic electronic insulating nature of sulfur and Li2S, and the substantial volume variation during charge/discharge processes. In this study, titanium nitride (TiN) powder was first prepared, and a carbon nanofiber/titanium nitride (CNF@TiN) composite nanofiber membrane was subsequently fabricated by electrospinning followed by pre-oxidation/carbonization treatment and employed as a functional interlayer between the separator and sulfur cathode. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) showed that the obtained TiN possessed a well-crystallized face-centered cubic structure. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) revealed that TiN particles were relatively uniformly dispersed and anchored within the three-dimensional interconnected CNF network. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses of the composite and the TiN powder confirmed the presence of Ti-N bonding, revealed N/O-containing functional groups on the carbon scaffold, and indicated only a thin oxidized layer on the TiN particle surface. Nitrogen adsorption-desorption analysis confirmed the porous character of the fibrous interlayers. Electrochemical tests showed that the cell equipped with the CNF@TiN interlayer delivered an initial discharge specific capacity of 1205 mAh·g-1 at 0.1 C and retained a reversible capacity of approximately 1010 mAh·g-1 after 100 cycles. At 0.2 C, the initial discharge specific capacity was approximately 1065 mAh·g-1, and approximately 875 mAh·g-1 was retained after 300 cycles, corresponding to a capacity retention of 82.2% and an average capacity decay of approximately 0.059% per cycle. Rate capability, cyclic voltammetry (CV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and galvanostatic charge-discharge measurements indicated that the CNF@TiN interlayer favors reversible sulfur-species conversion and improved interfacial reaction kinetics. The enhanced performance can be attributed to the physical confinement, electron-transport, and structural-support functions of the CNF network, together with the polar TiN interface, whose presence is consistent with restricted polysulfide migration and facilitated interfacial conversion. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing multifunctional interlayers integrating electrical conductivity, physical confinement, and interfacial regulation for Li-S batteries.

articles.titulo: Chemical and Biological Mobilization of Soil Phosphorus by ppk-Expressing Transgenic Rice (Oryza sativa L.).
articles.autores: Yang S, Wang M, … Yang L (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Phosphorus (P) availability in alkaline soils is constrained by the immobilization of legacy P, particularly through calcium phosphate precipitation. We used a confined soil-plant microcosm to examine how expression of the polyphosphate kinase gene (ppk) is associated with legacy P utilization in rice (Oryza sativa L.). We compared ppk-expressing transgenic rice (ETR) carrying single-copy (ETRS) and double-copy (ETRD) insertions with their isogenic wild type (WT), without P fertilization. Both transgenic lines had higher root organic acid release and acid phosphatase activity on day 30 and greater plant P acquisition by day 60 than WT; soil pH declined to a greater extent. On day 30, transgenic roots released more oxalate and malate, and their exudates mobilized more soil P than WT exudates in a separate incubation assay. These traits corresponded to greater depletion of the operationally defined HCl-P and NaOH-P pools. Bacterial profiles and PICRUSt2 predictions were descriptive because one pooled library per genotype precluded tests of genotype effects. Diffusive gradients in thin films (DGT) measurements revealed greater rhizosphere labile P in the ETRD early in plant growth, followed by a decline as plant P concentrations increased. This pattern was consistent with an early increase in P supply followed by plant-driven depletion. Net P acquisition in ETRD was 2.55 times that in WT, and ETRD exhibited 53% greater root biomass, while ETRS showed intermediate responses. Collectively, these results link enhanced plant P acquisition to greater P release in exudate incubation assays and higher acid phosphatase activity within this confined system.

articles.titulo: The Impact of Intra-Burst Energy Distribution on Volume Removal and Surface Quality in Laser Ablation of Stainless Steels Using Ultrashort Pulsed Lasers.
articles.autores: Obergfell D, Soldera F, … Lasagni AF (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Stainless-steel alloys are widely used in applications requiring high corrosion resistance and mechanical durability. For embossing tool fabrication, high-volume material removal with high surface quality is essential. Laser-based ablation offers an alternative to micromilling by enabling material removal without mechanical contact, thereby eliminating cutting tool wear and facilitating the fabrication of complex geometries. However, productivity must be increased without degrading surface quality, which plays a critical role in embossing tool wear behavior and lifetime. This study investigates the ablation efficiency and surface quality of AISI 304, AISI 420, and AISI 316Ti stainless steels using a 250 fs pulsed laser. Different fluence levels and burst configurations, including MHz, GHz, and Bi-burst, are examined, focusing on the influence of intra-burst energy distribution on material removal rate and surface quality. Surface morphology and roughness are characterized by optical, confocal, and scanning electron microscopy. The results show that removal rate, ablation efficiency, and surface roughness are strongly affected by the intra-burst energy distribution (positive or negative slopes). The highest removal rate of 5.74 mm3 min-1 was obtained using MHz bursts, whereas GHz bursts enabled surface roughness values Sa below 1 µm. Negative energy slopes generally reduced surface roughness in isolated MHz and GHz burst modes, while Bi-burst processing provided smooth surfaces over a wider range of slope conditions. All alloys followed similar trends, with AISI 316Ti exhibiting greater susceptibility to microhole formation under certain burst conditions.

articles.titulo: Organelle Volume Facilitates Spindle Positioning During C . elegans Female Meiosis.
articles.autores: Lazureanu DG, Krueger E, … McNally FJ (22 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cortical positioning of oocyte meiotic spindles is required for reducing chromosome number by segregating chromosomes into polar bodies. In C. elegans , kinesin-1 transports membrane-bound organelles inward into a central ball that is hypothesized to push the meiotic spindle outward. Using focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy, we found that the percent volume occupied by membrane-bound organelles was 28% in a mature oocyte that has completed endocytosis of the yolk precursor, vitellogenin, compared to 17% in a less mature oocyte that has not yet endocytosed vitellogenin. We therefore hypothesized that blocking endocytosis of vitellogenin would reduce the size of the central ball of organelles packed inward by kinesin-1 and limit outward movement of the spindle. Depletion of vitellogenin or proteins required for endocytosis resulted in a smaller central volume of kinesin-coated organelles and defective spindle positioning. A computer simulation of a simple exclusion model faithfully recapitulated wildtype and mutant spindle position phenotypes. These results support a volume exclusion model for positioning acentriolar meiotic spindles.

articles.titulo: A bacterial endosymbiont with a highly reduced genome forms extensive membrane contact sites with host organelles.
articles.autores: Leprich DJ, Aaron J, … McCutcheon JP (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Bacterial endosymbionts that establish long-term associations inside of host cells often lose a huge number of genes and become dependent on their hosts for essential cellular functions 1,2 . One such example is the mealybug endosymbiont Tremblaya princeps : its ~139-kb genome encodes only ~120 protein coding genes and lacks all recognizable genes for lipid and fatty acid synthesis, cell wall components, membrane transport, protein translocation, and transmembrane proteins, raising fundamental questions of how Tremblaya's cellular envelope is formed and maintained 3,4 . Here, using a combination of transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) of an entire endosymbiont-containing insect cell, we identified extensive and specific contacts between host cell mitochondria and Tremblaya . These contacts occurred at close membrane appositions and contained electron-dense bridge-like structures closely resembling classical eukaryotic membrane contact sites. Whole-cell segmentation showed that approximately 53% of host mitochondria were in contact with Tremblaya , with some mitochondria extensively wrapped by Tremblaya -associated membranes. Mitochondria in contact with Tremblaya were larger and contained proportionally greater cristae volume and surface density compared to non-contact mitochondria, exhibiting differences in both external and internal mitochondrial architecture. As membrane contact sites are well known to mediate lipid and metabolite exchange between membranes 5-10 , these findings suggest that direct interactions with host organelles may be a source of vital membrane and cellular components for endosymbionts that have lost the autonomous ability to produce and transport these molecules.

articles.titulo: In situ multimodal imaging reveals compartmentalization of reovirus replication factories.
articles.autores: Ďurinová E, Bily T, … Tuma R (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Avian reovirus (ARV) belongs to Reoviridae family of viruses with segmented dsRNA genomes. ARV is responsible for significant economic losses to the poultry industry by causing tenosynovitis and chronic respiratory disease in chickens. ARV virion exhibits an outer protein shell enclosing an inner core, which contains 10 unique dsRNA segments and multiple copies of viral polymerase. ARV assembly takes place in so-called viral factories (VFs). They are cytoplasmic membrane-less inclusions, which accumulate viral proteins and RNA and assist capsid assembly, genome packaging and replication. VFs also provide protection from the host cell defence mechanisms by sequestering viral RNA. Given the dense nature of VFs, little is known about ARV assembly and packaging intermediates. To determine the architecture of VFs across the different length scales and infection course, we employed a wide range of imaging methods. Our data reveal that spherical and fluid VF enriched in viral protein σNS become surrounded by σNS-depleted solid-like compartments at late stages of infection. We demonstrate that confocal Raman microscopy allows label-free imaging of VF composition. Volume electron microscopy, along with electron tomography (ET) and in situ cryo-ET, revealed that the inner phase of VF concentrates viral non-structural proteins and assists assembly of viral cores. The larger, RNA-filled and double-layered particles are assembled at the periphery of the inner fluid phase of VF, forming ordered virion arrays. This suggests that ARV VFs are functionally compartmentalized: the inner fluid phase assists RNA assortment and core particle assembly, whereas the peripheral phase is the site of RNA replication inside viral cores and virion completion.

articles.titulo: Fragment-Linked Purine Derivatives as Inhibitors of (p)ppGpp Synthetases: Design, Synthesis, and Structure-Activity Relationships.
articles.autores: Abdalrahman RAM, Erlitz KS, … Koch O (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The bacterial stringent response, mediated by the alarmone nucleotides (p)ppGpp, plays a central role in persistence of infections, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial tolerance, making (p)ppGpp synthetases attractive targets for novel antibacterial strategies/therapies. In this study, we report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of fragment-linked nucleobase derivatives targeting the RelA/SpoT homolog (RSH) enzymes. Guided by structural insights into adenine and guanine binding within small alarmone synthetase (SAS2/RelP), a series of purine-based compounds was developed to simultaneously occupy conserved nucleotide-binding regions. Initial linker-bridged analogues showed limited activity, primarily due to poor solubility, prompting the introduction of ribose-containing derivatives to improve physicochemical properties. Biochemical evaluation using HPLC-based assays revealed selective inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus SAS1, with the most potent compound displaying micromolar activity (IC50 = 1.8 µM), while little or no inhibition was observed for related SAS enzymes. Structure-activity relationship analysis highlights the importance of linker length and nucleobase positioning for enzyme selectivity. These findings establish fragment-linked nucleobase scaffolds as a promising starting point for the development of inhibitors targeting (p)ppGpp biosynthesis and the bacterial stringent response.

articles.titulo: Learning Spatially Adaptive Blur Representations for Stable Deconvolution in Electron Microscopy.
articles.autores: Kim K, Kim JY
articles.resumo_original: Spatially heterogeneous blur is frequently observed in practical electron microscopy (EM) acquisitions and can lead to nonuniform resolution across the field of view. Herein, we propose a patch-wise anisotropic blur-kernel estimation framework that performs uncertainty-aware regularized shift-variant deconvolution. The proposed method is not intended to replace standard scanning electron microscopy (SEM) acquisition optimization, such as focus correction, aperture selection, working-distance control, beam-current adjustment, or astigmatism correction. Rather, it is designed as a complementary post-acquisition restoration and quality-control tool for cases in which spatially heterogeneous blur remains after acquisition or when reacquisition is impractical. The method is expected to be most useful in high-magnification imaging, large-area SEM mapping, serial-section or volume EM workflows, and archived datasets, where local degradation may vary across the field of view. In controlled simulations with known references, the method improved restoration consistency relative to the evaluated global-point spread function (PSF) conditions. Application to experimental SEM images demonstrated exploratory feasibility, but the absence of matched blur-free references precluded conclusions regarding true spatial-resolution recovery or faithful morphology.

articles.titulo: Platelet-released polyphosphate controls thrombin generation.
articles.autores: Kurth JM, Zhang X, … McCarty OJT (4 autores)

articles.titulo: Comparative Evaluation of En Bloc Staining Protocols for Deep-Learning Segmentation of Dorsal Root Ganglia in SBF-SEM.
articles.autores: Borisovs V, Bossi M, … Cavaletti G (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The integration of deep learning algorithms into volumetric electron microscopy can be limited by biochemical sample preparation. En bloc staining protocols, emphasizing heavy-metal contrast, are optimized for the convenience of human visual interpretation. This study evaluates the suitability of three staining protocols for automated segmentation and 3D reconstruction of dorsal root ganglia (DRG): rOTO-based heavy-metal staining (Ellisman), standard transmission electron microscopy (TEM) staining (Palade), and uranyl-free en bloc staining (X-solution). U-Net-based deep learning models were applied to dorsal root ganglia (DRG) samples to segment nuclei, mitochondria, satellite glial cells (SGCs), and the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Quantitative segmentation performance was evaluated using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU) for each segmented structure group based on the comparison between the automated prediction masks and 30 manually annotated ground truth (GT) sections per staining protocol. Although the Ellisman-stained samples produced strong ultrastructural contrast, more false-positive and false-negative regions were observed for several structures.
